BURHAN:v4p406/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p406/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p406/r1.claim: The listed ما clauses include relative ما: what is harvested and stored, what was prepared for the seven years, what fathers married, and what people worship besides God.

BURHAN:v4p406/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p406/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p406/r2.claim: Maṣdariyya is divided into temporal, where ما is rendered as a duration, and non-temporal, where it combines with a verb as a verbal noun.
BURHAN:v4p406/r2.anchor: والثاني المصدرية وهي قسمان وقتية وغير وقتية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r2.claim: Shiqāʾ means hardship and badness of life, opposite saʿāda; the two forms may be transitive, as shown by the readings with ḍamma and lexicographic reports.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r2.anchor: الشقاء نكد العيش. وسوؤه. يقال منه: شقى يشقى شقاء وشقوة وشقاوة والسعادة ضده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r3.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says Hudhayl use سعده الله with the meaning أسعده الله.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r3.anchor: وذكر أن الفراء حكى أن هذيلا تقول: سعده الله بمعنى أسعده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r4.speaker: الجوهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r4.claim: Al-Jawharī distinguishes سعد بالكسر فهو سعيد from سعد فهو مسعود, by analogy with سلم فهو سليم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r4.anchor: وقال الجوهري: سعد بالكسر فهو سعيد، مثل سلم فهو سليم، وسعد فهو مسعود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r5.speaker: أبو نصر عبد الرحيم القشيري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r5.claim: Abū Naṣr al-Qushayrī says سعده الله yields مسعود, while أسعده الله yields مسعد.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p194/r5.anchor: وقال أبو نصر عبد الرحيم القشيري: ورد سعده الله فهو مسعود، وأسعده الله فهو مسعد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r1.claim: One analysis takes the exception as covering rational beings; those excluded from the Fire passage are sinful believers, while those excluded from Paradise are either they or the people of al-Aʿraf, who did not enter initially or remain as long as the first entrants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r1.anchor: أو تكون واقعة على من يعقل على مذهب من يرى وقوعها على من يعقل مطلقا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari answers that the exception concerns remaining in the Fire’s punishment and Paradise’s delight, not final residence: Hell includes cold, other punishments, divine wrath and humiliation; Paradise includes divine pleasure and unquantifiable gifts beyond its reward.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r2.anchor: هو استثناء من الخلود في عذاب النار، ومن الخلود في نعيم أهل الجنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r3.claim: He takes «إن ربك فعال لما يريد» as saying God inflicts the punishment He wills on Hell’s people and grants Paradise’s people an unending gift.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r3.anchor: أنه يفعل بأهل النار، ما يريد من العذاب، كما يعطي أهل الجنة عطاءه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari rejects the claim that the exception releases major sinners from Hell through intercession, arguing that its second occurrence refutes that reading; he invokes a report from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr that Hell will one day be empty after its inmates remain there for ages, and condemns using it to deny disbelievers’ eternal punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r4.anchor: قول المجبرة: المراد بالاستثناء خروج أهل الكبائر من النار بالشفاعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r5.claim: The report attributed to him says a day will come when Hell’s doors clap shut with no one inside, after its people have remained there for ages.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص: ليأتين على جهنم يوم تصفق فيه أبوابها ليس فيها أحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari’s exception can work for Hell if its people leave the Fire for zamharir, but his Paradise interpretation fails: receiving God’s pleasure and extra gifts does not stop them being eternal residents there.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212#2/r2.anchor: وأما ما ذكره من الاستثناء في أهل الجنة من قوله: خالدين، فلا يتمشى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the exception may be a recommended qualification of any statement, like the promise to enter the Sacred Mosque “if God wills”; as a condition, it need not be classed as connected or disconnected.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وأما قوله إلا ما شاء ربك، فقيل فيه: إن ذلك على طريق الاستثناء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212#2/r6.claim: Other proposed readings make «إلا» mean “and,” or “besides” as a disconnected exception; the latter means God adds what He wills and is attributed to al-Farraʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: إلا بمعنى الواو، فمعنى الآية: وما شاء الله زائدا على ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212#2/r7.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p212#2/r7.claim: Al-Farraʾ supports the disconnected “besides” interpretation by «عطاء غير مجذوذ»: an addition beyond their stated duration.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud, Talha ibn Musarrif, Ibn Waththab, al-Aʿmash, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs read «سُعِدوا» with a ḍamma on the sīn; the remaining canonical readers and majority use a fatḥa.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود، وطلحة بن مصرف، وابن وثاب، والأعمش، وحمزة، والكسائي، وحفص سعدوا بضم السين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r3.speaker: علي بن سليمان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r3.claim: Ali ibn Sulayman wondered that al-Kisaʾi, despite his Arabic expertise, read «سعدوا»; Abu Hayyan says there is no cause for surprise because it is transmitted from Ibn Masʿud and the other listed readers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r3.anchor: وكان علي بن سليمان يتعجب من قراءة الكسائي سعدوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r4.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r4.claim: Al-Kisaʾi cites «مسعود» as support for «سعدوا»; Abu Hayyan objects that the adjective may mean “a place in which one was made happy,” with «فيه» omitted.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r5.speaker: المهدوي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r5.claim: Al-Mahdawi treats «سعدوا» as based on «مسعود» but calls it rare and anomalous, since Arabic says «أسعده الله», not «سعده الله».
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r5.anchor: وقال المهدوي: من قرأ سعدوا فهو محمول على مسعود، وهو شاذ قليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r6.speaker: الثعلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r6.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi says «سعد» and «أسعد» have the same meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r6.anchor: وقال الثعلبي: سعد وأسعد بمعنى واحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r7.claim: «عطاء» is an accusative verbal noun meaning “giving,” as in describing God’s causing people to grow from earth as “growth.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r7.anchor: وانتصب عطاء على المصدر أي: أعطوا عطاء بمعنى إعطاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r8.claim: «غير مجذوذ» means uncut and continuing without end.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p213/r8.anchor: ومعنى غير مجذوذ: غير مقطوع، بل هو ممتد إلى غير نهاية

ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r8.claim: The Garden of the blessed is the Garden of fulfilled desires and pleasures, the garden of the soul.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r8.anchor: وأما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة ) أي جنة حصول المراد واللذات وهي جنة النفس

ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r9.claim: The blessed rise by God's will to higher gardens of the heart through witnessing the attributes, and of the spirit through vision, beyond anything the senses or imagination conceive.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r9.anchor: فيخرجون من ذلك إلى ما هو أعلى وأعلى من جنات القلب في مقام تجليات الصفات وجنات الروح في مقام الشهود

ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r10.claim: The tanwin may mark a type, and the exception may mean a wretched person leaves Fire for Paradise by purifying the soul of what blocked the way.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168/r10.anchor: وقد يحمل التنوين على النوعية ويؤول الاستثناء بخروج الشقي من النار بالترقي من مقامه إلى الجنة

THALABI:v5p189/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p189/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p189/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reads “as long as the heavens and earth” as the period from their beginning until their end.
THALABI:v5p189/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ما دامت السماوات والأرض من ابتدائها إلى وقت فنائها

THALABI:v5p189/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p189/r2.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v5p189/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says these are the heavens and earth of Paradise and Hell; anything overhead is a heaven and anything underfoot is earth.
THALABI:v5p189/r2.anchor: قال الضحاك: ما دامت سماوات الجنة والنار وأرضهما، وكل ما علاك فأظلك فهو سماء

THALABI:v5p189/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p189/r3.speaker: الحسين
THALABI:v5p189/r3.claim: Al-Husayn understands the phrase as the Hereafter lasting as long as the heavens and earth of this world endured.
THALABI:v5p189/r3.anchor: قال الحسين: أراد ما دامت الآخرة كدوام السماء والأرض في الدنيا

THALABI:v5p189/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p189/r4.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v5p189/r4.claim: The people of linguistic interpretation say Arabs use familiar expressions about enduring natural events to mean permanence; God addresses them in their customary idiom.
THALABI:v5p189/r4.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: العرب [ ... ] في معنى التأبيد والخلود

THALABI:v5p189/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p189/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p189/r5.claim: The author introduces two exceptions and reports a view that they concern people of monotheism whom God will bring out of Hell.
THALABI:v5p189/r5.anchor: ثم استثنى فقال: إلا ما شاء ربك اختلف العلماء في هذين الاستثناءين، من أهل الشقاوة أو من أهل السعادة

THALABI:v5p189/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p189/r8.speaker: أبو مجلز
THALABI:v5p189/r8.claim: Abu Majliz says the exception allows God to forgive some and spare them Hell; for the blessed, it refers to their continued stay in Paradise.
THALABI:v5p189/r8.anchor: وقال أبو مجلز: هو جزاؤه إلا أن يشاء ربك أن يتجاوز عنهم

THALABI:v5p189/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p189/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v5p189/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd says God explicitly describes the Paradise reward as unending but does not state what He ordained for the people of Hell.
THALABI:v5p189/r12.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: في هذه الآية أخبرنا بالذي أنشأ لأهل الجنة فقال: هذا غير مجذوذ

THALABI:v5p189/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p189/r13.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v5p189/r13.claim: Ibn Kaysan says the exception can mean either group's time in worldly life before reaching its final abode, or their detention in the interval between death and resurrection.
THALABI:v5p189/r13.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: إلا ما شاء ربك من الفريقين من تعميرهم في الدنيا

THALABI:v5p190/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p190/r1.speaker: الزجاج
THALABI:v5p190/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj gives a linguistic reading in which illa means “other than,” so permanence lasts except for what God wills beyond it.
THALABI:v5p190/r1.anchor: الزجاج: في هذه الآية أربعة أقوال: قولان منها لأهل اللغة

THALABI:v5p190/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p190/r2.speaker: الزجاج
THALABI:v5p190/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj's second linguistic explanation treats the exception as hypothetical: God could remove them, but has informed them that they remain forever.
THALABI:v5p190/r2.anchor: والقول الثاني: إنه استثنى من الإخراج وهو لا يريد أن يخرجهم منها

THALABI:v5p190/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p190/r3.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v5p190/r3.claim: One semantic interpretation makes the exception refer to the time spent at the graves and awaiting judgment.
THALABI:v5p190/r3.anchor: خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك من مقدار مواقفهم على رأس قبورهم وللمحاسبة

THALABI:v5p190/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p190/r4.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v5p190/r4.claim: Another semantic interpretation takes the exception as additional bliss for Paradise's people and additional punishment for Hell's people.
THALABI:v5p190/r4.anchor: إلا ما شاء ربك من زيادة النعيم لأهل النعيم، وزيادة العذاب لأهل الجحيم

THALABI:v5p190/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p190/r5.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v5p190/r5.claim: Al-Farra says God has willed the people of Hell and Paradise to remain in their abodes, and illa may function like waw, as in the verse about those who wronged.
THALABI:v5p190/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء: معناه: وقد شاء ربك خلود هؤلاء في النار وهؤلاء في الجنة، وإلا بمعنى الواو سائغ جائز في اللغة

THALABI:v5p190/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p190/r6.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v5p190/r6.claim: Al-Farra cites Abu Tharwan's poetry to show illa can mean “but,” and also glosses the exception phrase as “as God willed,” citing a verse about prior marriages.
THALABI:v5p190/r6.anchor: وأنشدني أبو ثروان: من كان أشرك في تفرق فالج

THALABI:v5p190/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p190/r7.speaker: أهل الكوفة، أبو عبيد، أبو حاتم
THALABI:v5p190/r7.claim: The Kufans read saʿidū with damma as passive, “made happy”; others use fatḥa by analogy with shaqū, preferred by Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim.
THALABI:v5p190/r7.anchor: وأما الذين سعدوا قرأ أهل الكوفة: (سعدوا) بضم السين أي رزقوا السعادة

THALABI:v5p190/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p190/r8.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v5p190/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak takes the exception as their time in Hell until they enter Paradise.
THALABI:v5p190/r8.anchor: الضحاك: إلا ما مكثوا في النار حتى أدخلوا الجنة

THALABI:v5p190/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p190/r9.speaker: أبو سنان
THALABI:v5p190/r9.claim: Abu Sinan says the exception means more than the lifespan of the heavens and earth, which is precisely eternal permanence.
THALABI:v5p190/r9.anchor: أبو سنان: إلا ما شاء ربك من الزيادة على قدر مدة دوام السماء والأرض

THALABI:v5p190/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p190/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p190/r10.claim: The author explains the promise of an undiminished gift as a reward that is never cut off.
THALABI:v5p190/r10.anchor: قال الله عطاء غير مجذوذ غير مقطوع

THALABI:v5p191/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p191/r1.speaker: وكيع بن الجراح
THALABI:v5p191/r1.claim: Wakiʿ ibn al-Jarrah accuses the Jahmiyya of rejecting four verses that affirm Paradise's lasting provision and reward, citing verses on uncut fruit, lasting food and shade, God's enduring bounty, and an unbroken gift.
THALABI:v5p191/r1.anchor: وكيع بن الجراح: كفرت الجهمية بأربع آيات من كتاب الله

SIBAWAYH:وليستتثنيتهبالتيتمنعالرفعحالهقب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وليستتثنيتهبالتيتمنعالرفعحالهقب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وليستتثنيتهبالتيتمنعالرفعحالهقب.claim: In the verse, خالدين is an accusative circumstantial participle, parallel to آخذين in 51:15–16 and فاكهين in 52:18.
SIBAWAYH:وليستتثنيتهبالتيتمنعالرفعحالهقب.anchor: فإن قلت قد جاء ^ ( وأما الذين ~~سعدوا ففى الجنة خالدين فيها ) ^

SIBAWAYH:وليستتثنيتهبالتيتمنعالرفعحالهقب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وليستتثنيتهبالتيتمنعالرفعحالهقب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وليستتثنيتهبالتيتمنعالرفعحالهقب.claim: In فيها زيد قائما فيها, the first locative phrase licenses قائما as a circumstantial accusative; if the first is treated as canceled, قائما فيها is instead parsed with the later locative.
SIBAWAYH:وليستتثنيتهبالتيتمنعالرفعحالهقب.anchor: وذلك قولك فيها زيد قائما فيها

SIBAWAYH:وليستتثنيتهبالتيتمنعالرفعحالهقب.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وليستتثنيتهبالتيتمنعالرفعحالهقب.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وليستتثنيتهبالتيتمنعالرفعحالهقب.claim: With an indefinite subject, قائم فيها can be an adjective, while an accusative circumstantial analysis is also allowed; in أخوك في الدار ساكن فيها, فيها modifies ساكن.
SIBAWAYH:وليستتثنيتهبالتيتمنعالرفعحالهقب.anchor: وتقول في النكرة في دارك ~~رجل قائم فيها فتجرى قائم على الصفة

SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r1.claim: Although khālidīn is an accusative circumstantial, the author rejects calling the state estimated: unlike 39:73, here permanence does not follow entry.
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: { خالدين }: منصوب على الحال المقدرة. قلت: ولا حاجة إلى قولهم مقدرة

SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r2.claim: ما is a temporal verbal noun, meaning the duration of their continuance; دام is complete, meaning remained.
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r2.anchor: قوله: { ما دامت } " ما " مصدرية وقتية، أي: مدة دوامهما. و " دام " هنا تامة لأنها بمعنى بقيت.

SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari applies the exception to eternity in punishment and bliss: Hell-dwellers also suffer cold and other torments, while Paradise-dwellers receive divine approval greater than its delights; he cites 9:72 and 11:108, with 11:107 as parallel.
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r3.anchor: أحدها: وهو الذي ذكره الزمخشري فإنه قال: " فإن قلت: ما معنى الاستثناء في قوله:

SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r4.claim: The Sheikh says al-Zamakhshari’s explanation may work for Hell-dwellers, who leave the Fire for the cold, but not for Paradise-dwellers, who never leave Paradise.
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r4.anchor: قال الشيخ: " ما ذكره في أهل النار قد يتمشى لأنهم يخرجون من النار إلى الزمهرير

SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r5.claim: The author finds that explanation invalid for both groups: even when Hell-dwellers suffer the cold, they remain in the Fire.
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r5.anchor: قلت: الظاهر أنه لا يصح فيهما؛ لأن أهل النار مع كونهم يعذبون بالزمهرير هم في النار أيضا.

SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r6.claim: A second view makes the exception refer to time: they remain except for the period God wills, so they do not remain there forever.
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r6.anchor: الثاني: أنه استثناء من الزمان الدال عليه قوله: " خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض "

SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r7.claim: A third view attaches the exception to being in the Fire or Paradise, allowing for the interval before people enter either place on Judgment Day.
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r7.anchor: الثالث: أنه من قوله: " ففي النار " و " ففي الجنة " ، أي: إلا الزمان الذي شاءه الله

SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r8.speaker: قتادة والضحاك
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r8.claim: If the exception concerns remaining in Hell, it can refer to sinful believers who leave it for Paradise; this is reported from Qatada, al-Dahhak, and others, with the miserable including unbelievers and sinners.
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r8.anchor: وهذا المعنى مروي عن قتادة والضحاك وغيرهما

SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r9.claim: The sinner’s departure can explain the exception for the miserable, but no blessed person enters Paradise and later ceases to remain there, so it does not explain the blessed side.
SAMIN-DURR:11:108/r9.anchor: وأما حق الطرف الآخر فلا يتأتى هذا التأويل فيه؛ إذ ليس منهم من يدخل الجنة ثم لا يخلد فيها.

SAMIN-DURR:11:108#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:108#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:108#2/r1.claim: عطاء is an accusative cognate object confirming the preceding sense of giving; it may be an ism-masdar, a masdar with extra letters omitted, or governed by an implied verb.
SAMIN-DURR:11:108#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { عطآء } نصب على المصدر المؤكد من معنى الجملة قبله؛ لأن قوله: " ففي الجنة خالدين " يقتضي

SAMIN-DURR:11:108#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:108#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:108#2/r2.claim: The full masdar is الإعطاء; alternatively it parallels shortened نبات in 71:17, or an implied verb may be understood as عطوت, meaning I received.
SAMIN-DURR:11:108#2/r2.anchor: والمصدر في الحقيقة الإعطاء على الإفعال، أو يكون مصدرا على حذف الزوائد كقوله: أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا

SAMIN-DURR:11:108#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:108#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:108#2/r3.claim: مجذوذ means cut off; جذاذ names fragments of gold, silver, or stone. The author sees a close relation to جَدّ and adduces related pairs عتا/عثا and كثب/كتب.
SAMIN-DURR:11:108#2/r3.anchor: والمجذوذ: المقطوع، ويقال لفتات الذهب والفضة والحجارة: " جذاذ " من ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:11:108#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:108#2/r4.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:11:108#2/r4.claim: Al-Raghib derives جَدّ from cutting level ground and connects vigorous travel, cutting cloth for repair, and جديد, originally something cut and extended to anything newly made.
SAMIN-DURR:11:108#2/r4.anchor: إلا أن الراغب جعل جد بالمهملة بمعنى قطع الأرض المستوية، ومنه " جد في سيره يجد جدا "

ZAJJAJ:v3p79/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p79/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p79/r4.claim: A fourth view applies the exception to the mentioned groaning: they have it except for other kinds of punishment; likewise Paradise includes delights both mentioned and unmentioned, which Zajjaj says the unbroken gift supports.
ZAJJAJ:v3p79/r4.anchor: وفيها قول رابع: أن الاستثناء وقع على أن لهم فيها زفيرا وشهيقا

ZAJJAJ:v3p79/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p79/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p79/r5.claim: Ghayra majdhūdh means not cut off, uninterrupted.

ZAJJAJ:v3p79/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p79/r6.speaker: النابعة
ZAJJAJ:v3p79/r6.claim: Al-Nābigha's lines describe swords cutting through armor, illustrating cutting and severance in Arabic usage.
ZAJJAJ:v3p79/r6.anchor:
قال النابعة
تقد السلوقي المضاعف نسجه. . . وتوقد بالصفاح نار الحباحب

ASAD-NOTES:11:108#n135/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:108#n135/r1.speaker: Razi and Manar XII, 161
ASAD-NOTES:11:108#n135/r1.claim: Razi and Manar XII, 161 explain the exception as God willing to give the people of Paradise a still greater reward.
ASAD-NOTES:11:108#n135/r1.anchor: God wills to bestow on them a yet greater reward (Razi; also Manar XII, 161)

ASAD-NOTES:11:108#n135/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:108#n135/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:108#n135/r2.claim: Asad considers it more probable that the exception means God opens for humanity a new and higher stage of evolution.
ASAD-NOTES:11:108#n135/r2.anchor: which to my mind is more probable - unless He opens up to man a new, yet higher stage of evolution.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Abu Amr, Asim in Abu Bakr's narration, and Ibn Amir read saʿidū with fatḥa on the sīn.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وابن عامر: سعدوا بفتح السين

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r2.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, and Hafs from Asim read saʿidū with ḍamma on the sīn.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم: سعدوا بضم السين

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r3.claim: Sibawayh's سعد يسعد سعادة is intransitive, like شقي; because it has no object, forming it as a passive is disfavored and makes the ḍamma reading heavy.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r3.anchor: حكى سيبويه: سعد يسعد سعادة فهو سعيد، وينبغي أن يكون غير متعد

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r4.claim: The ḍamma could reflect an unusual dialect or a فعل/فعّله alternation; مسعود does not prove it, since it may lose an augment like مجنون from أجنه الله.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r4.anchor: وأن مسعودا على سعدوا، ولا دلالة قاطعة على هذا، لأنه يجوز أن يكون مثل: أجنه الله فهو مجنون

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r5.claim: Al-Tirmah's لاقح means bearing pollination by attribution, not an augmented participle with deletion; the Qur'anic لواقح is the verbal form, unlike the nisba عاصفة/عاصف usage.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p378/r5.anchor: فإن قوله للاقح ليس على: ألقحتها الريح، فحذفت منها الزيادة كما حذف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r4.claim: Khālidīn is an accusative circumstantial expression denoting a state that is to come.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r4.anchor: وانتصاب خالدين على أنها حال مقدرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r5.claim: Mā is a temporal adverbial verbal noun, meaning for the duration that the heavens and earth endure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r5.anchor: وما مصدرية ظرفية أي: مدة دوام السموات والأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r6.claim: The duration signifies perpetuity, like Arabic expressions “as long as Thabīr stands” or “as long as a star shines,” without regard to whether either lasts forever.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r6.anchor: والمراد بهذا التوقيت التأييد كقول العرب: ما أقام ثبير وما لاح كوكب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r7.claim: Another view takes the heavens and earth as those of the afterlife, which endure forever; Quranic references support this view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: سموات الآخرة وأرضها وهي دائمة لا بد، يدل على ذلك يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسماوات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r8.claim: A view argues that the afterlife must include a heaven or other covering, since its inhabitants need something to shelter and shade them; whatever gives shade counts as a heaven.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r8.anchor: ولأنه لا بد لأهل الآخرة مما يقلهم ويظلمهم، إما سماء يخلقها الله، أو يظلهم العرش وكلما أظلك فهو سماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the heavens and earth return to their originating light and remain forever in the light of the Throne.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r9.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: أن السموات والأرض في الآخرة يردان إلى النور الذي أخذتا منه، فهما دائمتان أبدا في نور العرش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r10.claim: The apparent syntax makes the exception refer to a period within the time span of remaining in Hell or Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r10.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: إلا ما شاء ربك استثناء من الزمان الدال عليه قوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r11.claim: On that reading, the exception can be the interval on Judgment Day when the blessed and damned have not yet entered Paradise or Hell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r11.anchor: والمعنى: إلا الزمان الذي شاءه الله تعالى، فلا يكون في النار، ولا في الجنة، ويمكن أن يكون هذا الزمان المستثنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r13.claim: For Paradise, the exception could mark the time sinful believers or the people of al-Aʿrāf miss before entering, so they did not begin their unending stay with the first arrivals.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r13.anchor: لكن يمكن ذلك باعتبار أن يكون أريد الزمان الذي فات أهل النار العصاة من المؤمنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r14.claim: Another possible syntax attaches the exception to the implicit pronoun in the prepositional phrase or in khālidīn, with mā denoting a rational being or class.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p210#2/r14.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون استثناء من الضمير المستكن في الجار والمجرور، أو في خالدين، وتكون ما واقعة على نوع من يعقل

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r1.claim: Unlike the Hell passage, this verse does not mention the saved people's joy because the treatment of Hell serves warning and admonition.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r1.anchor: لم يذكر ها هنا أن لهم بهجة وسرورا كما ذكر في أهل النار

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r2.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, Hafs, and several early authorities read the verb passively; most of the seven readers use the active voice.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r2.anchor: قرءاة حمزة والكسائي وحفص ونسبت إلى ابن مسعود وطلحة بن مصرف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r3.speaker: علي بن سليمان
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r3.claim: Ali ibn Sulayman preferred the active reading and wondered how al-Kisai could read the passive despite his Arabic expertise.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r3.anchor: وكان يقول عجبا من الكسائي كيف قرأ

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r4.claim: Alusi rejects the criticism of al-Kisai: his reading is transmitted authentically, not based on opinion, and is not unique.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r4.anchor: ولم يقرأ بالرأي ولم يتفرد بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r5.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r5.claim: Al-Farra' says Hudhayl uses sa'adahu Allah with the meaning of as'adahu, supporting the transitive passive reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r5.anchor: وذكر أن الفراء حكى أن هذيلا تقول سعده الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r6.speaker: الجوهري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r6.claim: Al-Jawhari gives the active pattern sa'ida, fa-huwa sa'id, and the passive description mas'ud.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r6.anchor: وقال الجوهري سعد بالكسرة فهو سعيد مثل قولهم سلم فهو سليم وسعد فهو مسعود

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r7.speaker: القشيري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r7.claim: Al-Qushayri distinguishes sa'adahu Allah as mas'ud from as'adahu Allah as mus'ad.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r7.anchor: وقال أبو نصر عبد الرحيم القشيري ورد سعده الله تعالى فهو مسعود

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r8.claim: The contrast between active 'they were wretched' and passive 'they were made felicitous' intimates that granted felicity merits gratitude to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r8.anchor: وما ألطف الإشارة في - شقوا وسعدوا - على قراءة البناء للفاعل في الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r9.claim: The gift is not cut off or terminated; Ibn Qutayba notes forms with dhal or dal, with dhal more common.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r9.anchor: أي غير مقطوع عنهم ولا مخترم ومصدره الجذ

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r10.claim: Alusi prefers parsing 'gift' as a cognate accusative implied by being in Paradise and remaining there; alternatives make it a state or specification of divine willing.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r10.anchor: ونصب عطاءا على المصدرية من معنى الجملة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r11.claim: Other parses treat 'gift' as a state of an implied object of willing or a specification clarifying whether the gift can be cut off.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r11.anchor: وقيل هو نصب على الحالية من المفعول المقدر للمشيئة أو تمييز

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r12.claim: Calling the reward an unbroken gift emphasizes permanence and blocks the inference that the exception entails Paradise's end.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r12.anchor: مبالغة في التأبيد ودفعا لما يتوهم من ظاهر الاستثناء من الانقطاع

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r13.claim: Another explanation says the gift clause assures that the reward itself never ends, so the exception denotes successive blessings and God's pleasure, or a limitation at the beginning.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r13.anchor: وقيل إن ذلك لبيان أن ثواب أهل الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r14.claim: The Hell passage ends by saying God does as He wills, signaling that He may relieve some and leave others; Paradise instead closes with unending grace.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r14.anchor: ولهذا فرق في النظم بين التأبيد من حيث تمم الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r15.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r15.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir transmits al-Hasan's report that even if Hell's people remained as long as the sands of Alij, they would have a day when they leave.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r15.anchor: بما أخرجه ابن المنذر عن الحسن قال قال عمر لو لبث أهل النار

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r16.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r16.claim: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh transmits Abu Hurayra's report that a day will come when no one remains in Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r16.anchor: إسحاق بن راهويه عن أبي هريرة قال سيأتي على جهنم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r17.speaker: إبراهيم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r17.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh transmit Ibrahim's view that this is the Qur'an's most hopeful verse for Hell's inhabitants.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r17.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر وأبو الشيخ عن إبراهيم قال ما في القرآن آية أرجى لأهل النار

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r18.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r18.claim: Ibn Mas'ud predicts a time when Hell's doors will clap shut.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r18.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود ليأتين عليها زمان تصفق فيه أبوابها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r19.speaker: الشعبي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r19.claim: Al-Tabari transmits al-Sha'bi's saying that Hell is the faster of the two abodes to fill and the faster to decay.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p145#3/r19.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن الشعبي قال جهنم أسرع الدارين عمرانا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r1.claim: Alusi affirms the consensus that unbelievers remain eternally in Hell; decisive proofs outweigh reports of its emptying, the verse does not prove the contrary, and abrogation is unnecessary.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r1.anchor: وانت تعلم أن خلود الكفار مما أجمع عليه المسلمين ولا عبرة بالمخالف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r2.speaker: ابن الجوزي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r2.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi declared some reports fabricated, including the claim that Hell will empty of Adam's descendants and its doors clap like monotheists' houses.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r2.anchor: وقد نص ابن الجوزي على وضع بعضها كخبر عن عبد الله بن عمرو

ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r3.claim: Reports about Hell emptying do not overcome decisive evidence for unbelievers' eternal punishment; there is no need to claim this verse was abrogated.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r3.anchor: ولا يقاوم واحدا منها كثير من هذه الأخبار ولا دليل في الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r4.claim: The sequence gathers all souls, divides them into wretched and fortunate, then partitions the groups; al-Sharif al-Qayrawani's poem illustrates the pattern.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r4.anchor: وقد ذكر أن في الآية صيغة الجمع مع التفريق والتقسيم أما الجمع

ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r5.claim: Alusi cites the verse's general statement about every soul and the following division as a progression from gathering to classification.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p146/r5.anchor: في الآية صيغة الجمع مع التفريق والتقسيم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r1.claim: The successive fa particles continue the sequence, and the wording intimates that wretchedness and felicity were settled beforehand.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p147/r1.anchor: ومن هنا يعلم حال الفاءين فاء فمنهم وفاء فأما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200#2/r4.claim: For the blessed, the exception can mean the period they remain in Hell before entering Paradise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200#2/r4.anchor: وأما الاستثناء في أهل السعادة فيرجع إلى مدة لبثهم في النار قبل دخول الجنة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200#2/r5.claim: Another view says the exception for both groups is their time in worldly life and in the barzakh before their final destination.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: إلا ما شاء ربك من الفريقين من تعميرهم في الدنيا واحتباسهم في البرزخ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200#2/r6.claim: Another reading takes illā as 'apart from': they remain for the span of the heavens and earth, plus the additional duration God wills, which is their endless stay.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200#2/r6.anchor: من الزيادة على قدر مدة بقاء السموات والأرض، وذلك هو الخلود فيها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200#2/r7.claim: Some take illā to mean 'and'; the exception then affirms God's will that both groups remain in their respective abodes, as in 2:150.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p200#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: إلا بمعنى الواو، أي: وقد شاء ربك خلود هؤلاء في النار وهؤلاء في الجنة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r1.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read suʿidū with ḍamma on sīn and kasra on ʿayn, a passive meaning 'were granted happiness'; the other readers use fatḥa by analogy with shaqū.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص {سعدوا} بضم السين [وكسر العين]

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the exception is the time the blessed spend in Hell before entering Paradise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r2.anchor: قال الضحاك: إلا ما مكثوا في النار حتى أدخلوا الجنة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r3.claim: Qatāda says God knows what is excepted.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r4.claim: Ghayru majdhūdh means uncut or uninterrupted.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says God explicitly described the gift for Paradise's inhabitants as unending, without telling us what He wills for Hell's inhabitants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد: أخبرنا الله تعالى بالذي يشاء لأهل الجنة، فقال: {عطاء غير مجذوذ}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that a time will come when no one remains in Hell, after its inhabitants have stayed there for ages.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r6.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: ليأتين على جهنم زمان ليس فيها أحد، وذلك بعدما يلبثون فيها أحقابا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r7.claim: Abū Hurayra is reported to have said the same about a time when Hell has no one in it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r7.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه مثله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r8.claim: For Sunnis, if the report is established, it means none of the people of faith remains in Hell; the places of the unbelievers remain filled forever.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p201#2/r8.anchor: ومعناه عند أهل السنة إن ثبت: أن لا يبقى فيها أحد من أهل الإيمان. وأما مواضع الكفار

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r11.claim: The second exception refers to those same believers, separated from Paradise during punishment; a fixed starting point also qualifies perpetuity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r11.anchor: وهم المراد بالاستثناء الثاني فإنهم مفارقون عن الجنة أيام عذابهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r13.claim: Alternatively, Hell’s people sometimes move to the bitter cold or other torments, while Paradise’s people receive higher bliss such as divine pleasure, vision, and nearness to the Holy Presence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r13.anchor: أو لأن أهل النار ينقلون منها إلى الزمهرير وغيره من العذاب أحيانا، وكذلك أهل الجنة ينعمون بما هو أعلى من الجنة

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r14.claim: The exception may cover waiting for judgment, since the wording places them in Hell when the Day comes; if duration is unrestricted to that Day, it may cover worldly life and the barzakh.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-108/r14.anchor: أو من أصل الحكم والمستثنى زمان توقفهم في الموقف للحساب لأن ظاهره يقتضي أن يكونوا في النار حين يأتي اليوم

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-109/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-109/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-109/r4.claim: Unsevered gift explicitly says reward does not end and shows the exception does not mean its cessation; reward and punishment are phrased differently to mark permanence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-109/r4.anchor: غير مقطوع، وهو تصريح بأن الثواب لا ينقطع وتنبيه على أن المراد من الاستثناء في الثواب ليس الانقطاع

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-109/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-109/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-109/r5.claim: They read سعدوا as passive, from سعده الله, meaning God made them happy.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-109/r5.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص { سعدوا } على البناء للمفعول من سعده الله بمعنى أسعده

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-109/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-109/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-109/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ is accusative either as an emphatic verbal noun, or as a circumstantial accusative from Paradise.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:106-109/r6.anchor: و { عطاء } نصب على المصدر المؤكد أي أعطوا عطاء أو الحال من الجنة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r1.claim: Al-Biqāʿī glosses the fortunate as people who attain their aims and find their affairs made easy.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r2.claim: Paradise is already a religious certainty, and the fortunate dwell there eternally.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r2.anchor: أي التي صارت معلومة من الدين بالضرورة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r3.claim: The fortunate remain in Paradise forever, without end.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r3.anchor: على ما جرت به عادة العرب في إرادة التأبيد

BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r4.claim: The Arabs use the heavens-and-earth formula idiomatically to express endless duration.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r4.anchor: على ما جرت به عادة العرب في إرادة التأبيد لا آخر بمثل هذا

BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r5.claim: The stated exception does not cancel eternal bliss; the following assurance that the gift is unsevered is its strongest proof.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r5.anchor: وأدل دليل على ما قلت في الاستثناء

BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r6.claim: Unsevered means neither cut off, broken, divided, nor diminished; even a momentary interruption would make the gift severed or reduced.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r6.anchor: اي مقطوع ولا مكسور ولا مفصول

BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r7.claim: Ending with the unsevered gift firmly establishes permanence and comforts Paradise's people, in contrast to the people of Hell.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r7.anchor: وفي الختم بذلك من الجزم بالدوام طمأنينة لأهل الجنة زيادة في نعيمهم عكس ما كان لأهل النار

BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r8.speaker: أبو الحسن الرماني
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r8.claim: Al-Rummānī glosses zafīr as repeated voiced breathing and shahīq as a terrible prolonged inward sound; their roots suggest strain or length, while khālid means perpetual residence and dāʾim continuing duration.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r8.anchor: قال أبو الحسن الرماني : والزفير : ترديد النفس مع الصوت حتى تنتفخ الضلوع

BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r9.claim: The account of the two groups' final judgment strengthens the Prophet to carry out the whole mission, trusting God's support before the gathered people.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p581/r9.anchor: ولما أخبره تعالى بوقوع القضاء بتمييز الناس في اليوم المشهود إلى القسمين المذكورين على الحكم المشروح مرهبا ومرغبا

BURSEVI:v4p119/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p119/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p119/r4.claim: If the phrase means their coming to be in Hell, khālidīn is an anticipatory circumstantial from the pronoun implied in the locative's settlement clause.
BURSEVI:v4p119/r4.anchor: خالدين فيها مقيمين دائمين فيها حال مقدرة من ضمير الاستقرار في الظرف وهو قوله في النار هذا إن أريد حدوث كونهم في النار

BURSEVI:v4p119/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p119/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v4p119/r5.claim: Another grammatical view needs no anticipatory circumstantial: unlike 39:73, where permanence follows entry, the people here already abide in Hell.
BURSEVI:v4p119/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لا حاجة هنا إلى جعل الحال مقدرة كما في قوله تعالى : فادخلوها خالدين

BURSEVI:v4p119/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p119/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p119/r6.claim: Mā is a verbal noun particle whose clause functions as a temporal adverb; the phrase is an Arabic idiom for endless duration, since Arabs regarded heaven and earth as everlasting.
BURSEVI:v4p119/r6.anchor: ما مصدرية والمصدر المؤول قائم مقام الظرف

BURSEVI:v4p119/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p119/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p119/r7.claim: If duration is literally conditioned on heaven and earth, these are the everlasting afterlife heavens and earth; the cited verses describe the earth being changed and inherited by Paradise's people, who need shelter and ground.
BURSEVI:v4p119/r7.anchor: وإن أريد تعليق قرارهم فيها بدوام السموات والأرض فالمراد سموات الآخرة وأرضها

BURSEVI:v4p119/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p119/r8.speaker: حضرت شيخ قدس سره
BURSEVI:v4p119/r8.claim: The Shaykh says in the Futūḥāt that the heavens' and earth's permanence concerns their substance, not their form.
BURSEVI:v4p119/r8.anchor: حضرت شيخ قدس سره درفتوحات آورده كه دوام آسمان وزمين از حيثيت جوهر ايشان مرادست نه از حيثيت صورت ايشان

BURSEVI:v4p119/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p119/r9.speaker: أهل التأويل
BURSEVI:v4p119/r9.claim: The people of inward interpretation read the heavens as spirits and hearts, and the earth as souls and human embodiment.
BURSEVI:v4p119/r9.anchor: وقال أهل التأويل سموات الأرواح والقلوب وأرض النفوس والبشرية

BURSEVI:v4p119/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p119/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p119/r10.claim: The exception qualifies Hell's permanence because some sinful monotheists leave it; removing the rule for only part of the group suffices to validate the exception.
BURSEVI:v4p119/r10.anchor: استثناء من الخلود في النار لأن بعض أهل النار وهم فساق الموحدين يخرجون منها وذلك كاف في صحة الاستثناء

BURSEVI:v4p119/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p119/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p119/r11.claim: A person can combine misery and happiness from different perspectives; al-Najmiyya takes the exception to concern the wretched, who fall into two ranks, wretched and more wretched.
BURSEVI:v4p119/r11.anchor: كما قال في التأويلات النجمية : إلا ما شاء ربك من الأشقياء وذلك لأن أهل الشقاوة على ضربين شقي وأشقى

BURSEVI:v4p120/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p120/r1.speaker: الكسائي
BURSEVI:v4p120/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī accepts both saʿida and asʿada as Arabic forms, meaning that their happiness was decreed and they were created for it.
BURSEVI:v4p120/r1.anchor: من سعد بمعنى أسعد لغتان حكاهما الكسائي

BURSEVI:v4p120/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p120/r2.speaker: قتادة
BURSEVI:v4p120/r2.claim: Qatāda says God knows best what the exception means.

BURSEVI:v4p120/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p120/r3.speaker: الضحاك
BURSEVI:v4p120/r3.claim: Al-Dahhāk interprets the exception as their time in Hell before entering Paradise; duration can be limited by its starting point as well as its endpoint.
BURSEVI:v4p120/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك إلا ما مكثوا في النار حتى ادخلوا الجنة فإن التأبيد من مبدأ معين كما ينقص باعتبار الانتهاء فكذلك باعتبار الابتداء

BURSEVI:v4p120/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p120/r4.speaker: أبو السعود
BURSEVI:v4p120/r4.claim: Abū al-Suʿūd says that under a counterfactual reading the phrase is an accusative verbal noun of implied giving, meaning an unending gift; if it denotes spiritual bliss, it is a circumstantial accusative for the implied object of divine will.
BURSEVI:v4p120/r4.anchor: وقال المولى أبو السعود في تفسيره : إن حمل على طريقة التعليق بالمحال فقوله : عطاء غير مجذوذ نصب على المصدرية من معنى الجملة

BURSEVI:v4p120/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p120/r5.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v4p120/r5.claim: Some great masters say Paradise's inhabitants remain within Paradise's rank, while people of spiritual ascent pass beyond it.
BURSEVI:v4p120/r5.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : أهل الجنة يبقى في مرتبة الجنة وأهل الترقي يتجاوز ويترقى إلى ما فوقها

BURSEVI:v4p120/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p120/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p120/r6.claim: Al-Najmiyya divides the happy into the happy and happier: the first remain in Paradise's grades according to worship and servanthood, while the happier pass to stations of divine proximity through knowledge, piety, and love.
BURSEVI:v4p120/r6.anchor: أن أهل السعادة على ضربين سعيد وأسعد

BURSEVI:v4p120/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p120/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p120/r7.claim: A prophetic hadith says Paradise's people see those of ʿIlliyyīn as one sees a bright star in the sky, and names Abū Bakr and ʿUmar among them.
BURSEVI:v4p120/r7.anchor: إن أهل الجنة ليرون أهل العليين ، كما يرى أحدكم الكوكب الدري في أفق السماء

BURSEVI:v4p120/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p120/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p120/r8.claim: Those at the station of the truthful seat receive the most blissful station; by divine attraction they pass beyond Paradise to unity, whereas the path by works reaches the summit of spirituality but remains in duality at the Lote Tree and Garden of Refuge.
BURSEVI:v4p120/r8.anchor: فلهم الخروج من الجنة من جذبات العناية إلى عالم الوحدة والسر في هذا أن السالك يسلك بقدم المعاملات إلى أعلى مقام الروحانية

BURSEVI:v4p120/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p120/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p120/r9.claim: Neither a near angel nor a sent prophet crosses beyond that station without the Rafraf of divine attraction, which outweighs the works of humans and jinn and carries the servant to unity.
BURSEVI:v4p120/r9.anchor: فلا عبور عن هذا المقام للملك المقرب ولا للنبي المرسل إلا برفرف جذبة العناية فإنها توازي عمل الثقلين وبها يصل العبد إلى عالم الوحدة

BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r1.claim: At the station beyond Paradise there is no longer entry, exit, or exception; the exception refers to that station, and its gift has no end or change.
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r1.anchor: فما بقي هناك الدخول والخروج والاستثناء بقوله : {إلا ما شآء ربك} راجع إلى هذا المقام

BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r2.claim: The author, following oral teaching from his shaykh, says Paradise's people eventually reach a station unlike all earlier states, where the secret of primordial eternity appears in the mirror of everlastingness.
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r2.anchor: يقول الفقير : على ما تلقف من فم حضرة الشيخ العلامة أبقاه الله بالسلامة : إن أهل الجنة يصلون بمقتضى الاستثناء

BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r3.claim: The author distinguishes attached eternity before and after this manifestation: the special disclosure is at the endless end, beyond which there is no limit, while the period since entering Paradise preceded it.
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r3.anchor: وعند ذلك يظهر سر الأزل في مرآة الأبد فكما أن مبدأ التعينات

BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r4.claim: He compares this disclosure with the total annihilation attained by saints in worldly life after exhausting the spiritual secrets of acts, attributes, and essence available at their station.
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r4.anchor: ونظير هذا هو ما يصل إليه أهل الفناء الكلي في الدنيا وذلك أنهم استوفوا حظهم من الأرزاق المعنوية

BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r5.claim: The same secret applies to Hell's people as people of majesty in the station of singularity, without Paradise's marriage and pleasures; Paradise's people are people of beauty and the station of attributes, with its delights.
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r5.anchor: ثم السر المذكور المنسوب إلى أهل الجنة والعليين جار على أهل النار لكنهم أهل الجلال ومقامهم مقام الفردية

BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r6.claim: Paradise's people manifest through attributes, with essence hidden within manifestation; Hell's people have hiddenness without manifestation, while perfected knowers have boundless scope in both abodes.
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r6.anchor: فالفرق بين أهل الجنة وأهل النار أن لأهل الجنة ظهورا بالصفات وفي الظهور بطون

BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r7.claim: The spiritually near know the righteous' states and stations, while the righteous are veiled from them; likewise the righteous know the people of the left, who are veiled from the righteous, across worldly life, the barzakh, and the afterlife.

BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r8.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r8.claim: A great master says that after the body's prison ends, an elevated spirit crosses one barzakh, while another crosses more; the excerpt ends before completing the account.
BURSEVI:v4p120#2/r8.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : إن الروح بعد خلاصه من حبس البدن إن كان علويا بعضه يقطع برزخا وبعضه أكثر

DURR-FULL:v4p475/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the wretched as major sinners from the Muslim community: punishment is temporary, intercession removes them, and the exception covers their time in Hell.
DURR-FULL:v4p475/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: هاتان من المخبآت قول الله {فمنهم شقي وسعيد}

DURR-FULL:v4p476/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r2.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet said God may will to remove some of the wretched from Hell and admit them to Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r2.anchor: عن جابر رضي الله عنه قال: قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم {فأما الذين شقوا} إلى قوله {إلا ما شاء ربك} قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن شاء الله

DURR-FULL:v4p476/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r3.speaker: خالد بن معدان
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r3.claim: Khalid ibn Maʿdan applies the exception to monotheists among the Muslim community.
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r3.anchor: عن خالد بن معدان في قوله {إلا ما شاء ربك} قال: إنها في التوحيد من أهل القبلة

DURR-FULL:v4p476/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r4.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak likewise says the exception is for people of the Muslim community whom God excepts.
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك {إلا ما شاء ربك} قال: إلا ما استثنى من أهل القبلة

DURR-FULL:v4p476/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r5.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله الأنصاري أو أبو سعيد الخدري أو رجل من أصحاب رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r5.claim: A Companion, identified uncertainly as Jabir, Abu Saʿid, or another Companion, says this exception governs Qur’anic statements that people dwell forever.
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r5.anchor: عن أبي نضرة عن جابر بن عبد الله الأنصاري أو عن أبي سعيد الخدري أو رجل من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v4p476/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r7.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak says the happy are people removed from Hell to Paradise; the exception is their time in Hell before entering.
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله {وأما الذين سعدوا} الآية قال: هو

DURR-FULL:v4p476/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r8.speaker: سنان
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r8.claim: Sinnan says God excepted the people of monotheism, then affirmed their gift as uninterrupted.
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r8.anchor: عن سنان قال: استثنى في أهل التوحيد ثم قال {عطاء غير مجذوذ}

DURR-FULL:v4p476/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says every Garden has its own heaven and earth.
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ما دامت السماوات والأرض} قال: لكل جنة سماء وأرض

DURR-FULL:v4p476/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r10.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r10.claim: Al-Suddi identifies these as the heaven and earth of Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r10.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {ما دامت السماوات والأرض} قال: سماء الجنة وأرضها

DURR-FULL:v4p476/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r11.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r11.claim: Al-Hasan says another heaven and earth replace these, and Paradise lasts as long as those remain.
DURR-FULL:v4p476/r11.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله {ما دامت السماوات والأرض} قال: تبدل سماء غير هذه السماء وأرض غير هذه الأرض

DURR-FULL:v4p477/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p477/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p477/r1.claim: Al-Hasan describes the seven heavens and earths being cleansed and transformed into a shining white-silver earth for Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v4p477/r1.anchor: عن الحسن قال: إذا كان يوم القيامة أخذ الله السموات السبع والأرضين السبع فطهرهن من كل قذر ودنس وفصيرهن أرضا بيضاء فضة نورا يتلألأ

DURR-FULL:v4p477/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p477/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p477/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says God wills the damned to remain eternally in Hell and the blessed eternally in Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v4p477/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {إلا ما شاء ربك} قال: فقد شاء ربك أن يخلد هؤلاء في النار وأن يخلد هؤلاء في الجنة

DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r1.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says the exception for the blessed was later abrogated through 4:122, establishing everlasting Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r1.anchor: وقوله {وأما الذين سعدوا} الآية قال: فجاء بعد ذلك من مشيئة الله ما نسخها فأنزل بالمدينة

DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says God excepted the Fire’s consuming of them.
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {إلا ما شاء ربك} قال: استثنى الله أمر النار أن تأكلهم

DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r8.claim: Qatada leaves the outcome to God, saying He knows how His will has taken effect.
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r8.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {إلا ما شاء ربك} قال: الله أعلم بمشيئته على ما وقعت

DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says God specifies an unbroken gift for Paradise’s people but does not disclose what He wills for Hell’s people.
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r9.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال: قد أخبر الله بالذي شاء لأهل الجنة فقال {عطاء غير مجذوذ} ولم يخبرنا بالذي يشاء لأهل النار

DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r10.speaker: أبو وائل
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r10.claim: Abu Waʾil answered Qur’anic questions by saying God expressed through the passage what He intended.
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r10.anchor: عن أبي وائل أنه كان إذا سئل عن الشيء من القرآن قال: قد أصاب الله به الذي أراد

DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains ghayr majdhudh as uncut or uninterrupted.
DURR-FULL:v4p477#2/r12.anchor: وفي قوله {غير مجذوذ} قال: غير مقطوع

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r1.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak, reporting from Ibn Abbas, says the blessed are those who come after the misery they had experienced.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قوله : واما الذين سعدوا يعني بعد الشقاء الذي كانوا فيه

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the exception concerns monotheists who return to Paradise after punishment; both exceptions concern them, while polytheists remain in Hell without dying or leaving.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r2.anchor: عن الحسن قوله : واما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة خالدين فيها مادامت السماوات والارض الا ماشاء ربك يقول اهل السعادة في الجنة خالدين فيها

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r3.claim: The exception applies to those who remain in the Fire until they are brought out.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r3.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان في قوله : واما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة خالدين فيها وقع الاست ثناء علي من بقى في النار حتى يخرجون منها

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r4.speaker: أبو سنان عن أبي مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r4.claim: Abu Malik says God's will is their abiding in Paradise, followed by the assurance of an uncut gift.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي مالك عن أبي سنان في قوله : واما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة خالدين فيها الا ماشاء ربك ومشيئته خلودهم فيها

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says the exception allows for those who leave Hell for Paradise: they abide in Paradise except for the time spent in Hell before entering it.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك بن مزاحم قوله : الا ماشاء ربك قال وهي ايضا في الذين يخرجون من النار فيدخلون الجنة يقول خالدين في الجنة مادامت السماوات والارض

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، أبو العالية، مجاهد، الربيع بن أنس، النضر بن عربي، قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the gift as one that is not cut off; the same explanation is reported from Abu al-Aliyah, Mujahid, al-Rabi ibn Anas, al-Nadr ibn Arabi, and Qatada.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2087#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : عطاء غير مجذوذ يقول : عطاء غير مقطوع وروى عن ابي العالية ومجاهد والربيع بن انس والنضر بن عربي وقتادة نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2088/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2088/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2088/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the gift will not be diminished at all.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2088/r1.anchor: عن الحسن عطاء غير مجذوذ قال : لا ينقص منه شئ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r1.claim: The phrase ‘as long as the heavens and earth endure’ signifies perpetuity as a proverbial expression; the familiar heavens and earth will perish, or it can mean the heavens and earth of the afterlife.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r1.anchor: ومعنى { ما دامت السماوات والأرض } التأييد لأنه جرى مجرى المثل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r2.claim: The exception may qualify the times covered by ‘as long as,’ thereby also excluding some inhabitants by implication; this fits the usual nonrational sense of ما.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r2.anchor: استثناء من الأزمان التي عمها الظرف في قوله : { ما دامت }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r3.claim: Alternatively, the exception may qualify the pronoun ‘abiding’; ما often refers to rational beings, as in ‘whatever women are lawful to you.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون استثناء من ضمير { خالدين } لأن { ما } تطلق على العاقل كثيرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r6.claim: One possible sense is the first period of the Resurrection, when unrepentant sinful believers enter punishment until God forgives them, with or without intercession.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r6.anchor: وأما الاستثناء الثاني الواقع في جانب { الذين سعدوا } فيحتمل معنيين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r7.speaker: أنس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r7.claim: Anas’s sound hadith describes people entering Hell until they become like charcoal, then being brought out and admitted to Paradise as the ‘Jahannamiyyun.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r7.anchor: في الصحيح من حديث أنس : ( يدخل ناس جنم حتى إذا صاروا كالحممة أخرجوا وأدخلوا الجنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r8.claim: Alternatively, the exception warns against imagining that anyone has a claim to bliss binding on God; Paradise is a manifestation of divine grace and mercy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p165/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن يقصد منه التحذير من توهم استحقاق أحد ذلك النعيم حقا على الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r1.claim: A will-conditioned exception does not mean God will enact it; it means only that the exception would occur if He willed it. His promises show He will not remove Paradise’s people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r1.anchor: وليس يلزم من الاستثناء المعلق على المشيئة وقوع المشيئة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r2.claim: Once admitted to Paradise, its people abide forever and their bliss never ends; this is the meaning of the gift that is not cut off.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r2.anchor: فهم إذا أدخلوا الجنة كانوا خالدين فيها فلا ينقطع عنهم نعيمها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r3.anchor: وهو معنى قوله : { عطاء غير مجذوذ } . والمجذوذ : المقطوع .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r4.claim: The majority read saʿidu with fatḥa on the sīn.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r5.speaker: حمزة، والكسائي، وحفص عن عاصم، وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r5.claim: These readers use ḍamma on the sīn, treating the verb as passive though its base is intransitive: it means ‘made happy.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r5.anchor: وقرأه حمزة ، والكسائي ، وحفص عن عاصم ، وخلف بضم السين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r6.claim: The passive reading is explained by treating an intransitive verb as transitive in the sense of someone being made to acquire a quality, as in جن فلان.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r6.anchor: على معاملة القاصر معاملة المتعدي في معنى فعل به ما صيره صاحب ذلك الفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r7.claim: Another explanation is that سعد is transitive in the Hudhayl and Tamim dialects, meaning ‘God made him happy.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r7.anchor: وقيل : سعد متعد في لغة هذيل وتميم ، يقولون : سعده الله بمعنى أسعده .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r8.claim: A further analysis derives the form from أُسعدوا by dropping the augmenting hamza, as in مجنوب and مسعود.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p167/r8.anchor: وخرج أيضا على أن أصله أسعدوا ، فحذف همز الزيادة كما قالوا مجنوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r1.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r1.claim: The exception may be a conventional conditional appended to any statement, like the promise to enter the Sacred Mosque safely, rather than a connected or disconnected exception.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r1.anchor: فقيل فيه: إن ذلك على طريق الاستثناء الذي ندب الشرع إلى استعماله في كل كلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r2.claim: One view takes the exception as a limit on the duration: Hell and its inhabitants eventually perish and its doors close.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو استثناء من طول المدة، وذلك على ما روي من أن جهنم تخرب ويعدم أهلها وتغلق أبوابها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the extinction claim flawed; reports from Ibn Masʿud and others concern the highest level reserved for sinful believers, called Hell by extension.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r3.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا قول مختل، والذي روي ونقل عن ابن مسعود وغيره إنما هو الدرك الأعلى المختص بعصاة المؤمنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r4.speaker: قتادة والضحاك وأبو سنان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r4.claim: The exception may concern sinful believers released from the Fire after a time; on this reading, the wretched include both unbelievers and sinful believers, and the exception qualifies their abiding.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r4.anchor: وهذا قول قتادة والضحاك وأبي سنان وغيرهم، وعلى هذا فيكون قوله: فأما الذين شقوا عاما في الكفرة والعصاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r5.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r5.claim: Another view treats illā as wāw, meaning that God may add something beyond the stated duration.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r5.anchor: وقيل: إلا بمعنى الواو، فمعنى الآية: وما شاء الله زائدا على ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r6.claim: The cited poem can witness illā used as “and” if its poet believed even the Pleiades and the world would perish; a materialist poet would mean ordinary exception and provide no proof.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r6.anchor: وهذا البيت يصح الاستشهاد به على معتقدنا في فناء الفرقدين وغيرهما من العالم، وأما إن كان قائله من دهرية العرب فلا حجة فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r7.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads illā as “apart from,” a disconnected exception equivalent to siwā; he takes the exception as adding to the duration.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r7.anchor: وهذا قول الفراء، فإنه يقدر الاستثناء المنقطع ب «سوى» وسيبويه يقدره ب «لكن»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r8.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r8.claim: Sibawayh renders the disconnected exception with “but,” unlike al-Farrāʾ’s “apart from.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r8.anchor: وهذا قول الفراء، فإنه يقدر الاستثناء المنقطع ب «سوى» وسيبويه يقدره ب «لكن»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r9.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r9.claim: The added duration may be punishment of kinds unknown to people, such as zamharīr.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r9.anchor: وقيل سوى ما أعده لهم من أنواع العذاب مما لا يعرف كالزمهرير ونحوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r10.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r10.claim: Another proposal excepts the period they passed in worldly life from the duration measured by the heavens and earth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p208/r10.anchor: وقيل استثناء من مدة السماوات: المدة التي فرطت لهم في الحياة الدنيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r1.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r1.claim: The exception may refer to the barzakh between this world and the next.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r1.anchor: وقيل في البرزخ بين الدنيا والآخرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r2.claim: It may refer to the intervals between groups entering Hell, since they enter in successive companies.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r2.anchor: وقيل: في المسافات التي بينهم في دخول النار، إذ دخولهم إنما هو زمرا بعد زمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r3.speaker: أبو نضرة عن جابر أو أبي سعيد الخدري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r3.claim: A report transmitted by Abū Naḍra from Jābir or Abū Saʿīd takes the exception from “in the Fire” as a delay before entry.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r3.anchor: وهذا قول رواه أبو نضرة عن جابر أو عن أبي سعيد الخدري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r4.claim: The statement that God does whatever He wills draws attention to His power.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r4.anchor: ثم أخبر منبها على قدرة الله تعالى بقوله: إن ربك فعال لما يريد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r5.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم عن أبي بكر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r5.claim: These readers pronounce saʿidū with fatḥa on the sīn; it is an intransitive verb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم- في رواية أبي بكر- «سعدوا» بفتح السين، وهو فعل لا يتعدى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r6.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وعاصم عن حفص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r6.claim: They pronounce saʿidū with ḍamma on the sīn, a reading Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls anomalous.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r6.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وعاصم- في رواية حفص- «سعدوا» بضم السين، وهي شاذة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r7.claim: The form masʿūd does not prove the ḍamma reading: it can be a passive derived from asʿada after dropping the augment, like maḥbūb and majnūn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r7.anchor: ولا حجة في قولهم: مسعود، لأنه مفعول من أسعد على حذف الزيادة كما يقال: محبوب، من أحب، ومجنون من أجنه الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود وطلحة بن مصرف وابن وثاب والأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿud, Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, Ibn Waththāb, and al-Aʿmash also read the verb with ḍamma on the sīn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r8.anchor: وبضم السين قرأ ابن مسعود وطلحة بن مصرف وابن وثاب والأعمش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r9.claim: The earlier exception proposals also apply to the blessed, apart from Hell’s destruction and taking the exception from “in the Fire”; here one may except the time sinful believers spend in Hell.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r9.anchor: ويزيد هنا قول: أن يكون الاستثناء في المدة التي يقيمها العصاة في النار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r10.claim: ʿAṭāʾan is accusative as a verbal noun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r10.anchor: وقوله: عطاء غير مجذوذ، نصب على المصدر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r11.claim: Majdhūdh means cut off; jadhdh, jadd, and ḥazz all mean cutting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r11.anchor: و «المجذوذ» : المقطوع. و «الجذ» : القطع وكذلك «الجد» وكذلك «الحز»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r12.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r12.claim: Masʿūd may originally have described a place as fortunate, then become a personal name.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r12.anchor: وقد قيل في مسعود: إنما أصله الوصف للمكان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r13.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r13.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says Hudhayl used saʿadahu to mean asʿadahu, “God made him fortunate.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p209/r13.anchor: وذكر أن الفراء حكى أن هذيلا تقول: سعده الله بمعنى أسعده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r1.claim: The fortunate are the followers of the messengers, and Paradise is their home.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r2.claim: The people of Paradise remain there forever; the exception means their continuing bliss is dependent on God’s will and gracious favor, not something independently obligatory upon Him. He inspires their praise as naturally as breathing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r2.anchor: معنى الاستثناء هاهنا: أن دوامهم فيما هم فيه من النعيم، ليس أمرا واجبا بذاته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r3.speaker: الضحاك، والحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Hasan al-Basri say the exception concerns monotheist sinners who had been in Hell and were then brought out.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك، والحسن البصري: هي في حق عصاة الموحدين الذين كانوا في النار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وأبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Abu al-Aliyah, and others gloss the gift as uncut or unending; this closes off any inference of cessation after the mention of God’s will.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir contrasts punishment, subject to God’s will and grounded in His justice and wisdom, with the reassurance of an unbroken gift; he links the passage to 11:107 and 21:23.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r5.anchor: كما قال {لا يسأل عما يفعل وهم يسألون} [الأنبياء:23]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r6.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r6.claim: The Prophet is quoted declaring that Paradise’s people and Hell’s people have everlasting residence without death; a report in both Sahih collections adds that the people of Paradise never die, age, fall ill, or suffer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p352/r6.anchor: وفي الصحيحين (4) أيضا: "فيقال (5) يا أهل الجنة، إن لكم أن تعيشوا فلا تموتوا أبدا

JISHUMI:v5p3566/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r10.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r10.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, and Hafs from Asim read سُعدوا with ḍamma; the others use fatḥa in parallel with شقوا.
