JISHUMI:v5p3566/r10.anchor: حمزة، والكسائي، وحفص عن عاصم: سعدوا بضم السين

JISHUMI:v5p3566/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r11.claim: Ḍamma is explained as deletion of the augment in أسعدوا, since the verb is intransitive; سعد and أسعد are synonymous, like forms where an augment is removed.
JISHUMI:v5p3566/r11.anchor: وإنما جاز ضم السين؛ لأنه على حذف الزيادة من أسعدوا

JISHUMI:v5p3567/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r4.claim: عطاء is accusative as a verbal noun meaning He gave a gift and also functions circumstantially; خالدين is likewise circumstantial and accusative.
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r4.anchor: نصب على المصدر، أي: أعطاهم عطاء، فهو حال

JISHUMI:v5p3567/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r13.claim: The happy remain in Paradise permanently, except as God wills; their gift is uncut, as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Dahhak explain.
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r13.anchor: وأما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة خالدين فيها

JISHUMI:v5p3567/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r14.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Dahhak gloss غير مجذوذ as not cut off.
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r14.anchor: غير مجذوذ أي: غير مقطوع، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والضحاك

JISHUMI:v5p3567/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r15.claim: In response to the objection that reward and punishment are eternal, he gives two views: these very heavens and earth, or an expression of indefinitely long duration.
JISHUMI:v5p3567/r15.anchor: اختلف العلماء فيه على قولين: الأول: المراد بالسماوات والأرض هن هذه السماوات والأرض بعينها

JISHUMI:v5p3569/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r1.claim: One view treats the exception as possible expulsion without intent: God could expel them but ruled they remain; al-Hasan says the exception emphasizes that God willed their permanence.
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r1.anchor: وسادسها: أنه استثناء من الإخراج، وهو لا يريد إخراجهم

JISHUMI:v5p3569/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r2.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the exception concerns added bliss for Paradise's people and added torment for Hell's people.
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r2.anchor: وسابعها: أن الاستثناء وقع على الزيادة

JISHUMI:v5p3569/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes إلا as و, a common usage; the cited verse then means neither wrongdoers are exempt, and both groups remain forever.
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r3.anchor: بمعنى الواو، وذلك شائع في اللغة

JISHUMI:v5p3569/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r4.claim: For those who distinguish the groups, one reading has God release monotheists from Hell; Abu Majliz says He may forgive them before entry and may delay the happy before admitting them to Paradise.
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r4.anchor: أن يخرج أهل التوحيد منها. روي ذلك عن ابن عباس وقتادة

JISHUMI:v5p3569/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says God specified what He wills for Paradise's people as an uncut gift, but did not specify His will for Hell's people.
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r5.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: أخبرنا بالذي يشاء لأهل الجنة فقال

JISHUMI:v5p3569/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r6.speaker: الضحاك
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says the exception is time in Hell before entry to Paradise; the author rejects this because the clauses for both groups have the same structure, so permanence for one entails it for the other.
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r6.anchor: وعن الضحاك: إلا ما مكثوا في النار حتى أدخلوا

JISHUMI:v5p3569/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r7.claim: Another view makes the exception disconnected, meaning but for an increase, as in the phrase except Iblis.
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r7.anchor: هذا الاستثناء منقطع، وأكثر ما يكون ذلك كقوله

JISHUMI:v5p3569/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r10.claim: The uncut gift proves Paradise lasts forever, contrary to Jahm; both verses support eternal residence, with stronger emphasis in this phrase.
JISHUMI:v5p3569/r10.anchor: ويدل قوله:عطاء غير مجذوذ على دوام الجنة

JISHUMI:v5p3571/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3571/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3571/r1.claim: Reading these verses as ending the afterlife of Paradise and Hell is false by consensus and necessary religious knowledge: their inhabitants abide forever; dispute concerns grave sinners.
JISHUMI:v5p3571/r1.anchor: فباطل بالإجماع، ومما علم من دين الرسول ضرورة أن أهل الجنة يخلدون، وأن الكفار يخلدون، وإنما الخلاف في الفساق

JISHUMI:v5p3571/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3571/r2.speaker: وكيع بن الجراح
JISHUMI:v5p3571/r2.claim: Wakiʿ says the Jahmiyya disbelieved by rejecting four verses about unending divine rewards: 56:33, 13:35, 16:96, and this verse; the commentator calls their rejection clear unbelief.
JISHUMI:v5p3571/r2.anchor: وقال وكيع بن الجراح: كفرت الجهمية بأربع آيات من كتاب الله تعالى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r4.claim: One explanation takes the heavens and earth literally as the everlasting created heavens and earth of the next life.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r4.anchor: أحدهما : أن تراد سموات الآخرة وأرضها وهي دائمة مخلوقة للأبد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r5.claim: The author supports afterlife heavens with the transformed earth in 14:48 and the Garden inheriting earth in 39:74; the afterlife needs something to support and shade its people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r5.anchor: والدليل على أن لها سموات وأرضا قوله تعالى : { يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r6.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is an idiom of permanence, like ‘as long as Taʿār remains,’ ‘as long as Thabīr stands,’ and ‘as long as a star shines.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r6.anchor: والثاني أن يكون عبارة عن التأييد ونفي الانقطاع . كقول العرب : ما دام تعار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r7.claim: The exception does not shorten eternal residence: people of Hell may suffer freezing cold and other torments besides fire, including God’s wrath and humiliation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r7.anchor: وذلك أن أهل النار لا يخلدون في عذاب النار وحده ، بل يعذبون بالزمهرير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r8.claim: People of the Garden receive more than its pleasures: God’s approval and further gifts beyond recompense, whose full nature only He knows.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r8.anchor: وكذلك أهل الجنة لهم سوى الجنة ما هو أكبر منها وأجل موقعا منهم ، وهو رضوان الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r10.claim: The unsevered gift confirms that the exception concerns gifts beyond the Garden’s ordinary reward, not an end to eternal residence.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r10.anchor: فهو المراد بالاستثناء . والدليل عليه قوله : { عطاء غير مجذوذ }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r12.speaker: المجبرة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r12.claim: The author rejects the Mujabbira claim that the exception means major sinners leave Hell through intercession; he says the second exception disproves it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p405/r12.anchor: فإن الاستثناء الثاني ينادي على تكذيبهم ويسجل بافترائهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p406/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p406/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p406/r1.claim: A report attributed to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr says that after they remain for ages, a day comes when Hell’s doors clap shut with no one inside.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p406/r1.anchor: ليأتين على جهنم يوم تصفق فيه أبوابها ليس فيها أحد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p406/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p406/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p406/r2.claim: The author condemns those who use the report to claim unbelievers do not remain eternally in Hell, calling that a manifest error.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p406/r2.anchor: وقد بلغني أن من الضلال من اغتر بهذا الحديث ، فاعتقد أن الكفار لا يخلدون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p406/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p406/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p406/r3.claim: If the report is sound, it means the damned leave the heat of fire for freezing torment; this is how Hell can be empty and its doors clap shut.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p406/r3.anchor: ولئن صح هذا عن ابن العاص ، فمعناه أنهم يخرجون من حر النار إلى برد الزمهرير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p406/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p406/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p406/r4.claim: The author adds a polemical jab that Ibn ʿAmr’s fighting ʿAlī with his two swords should have occupied him too much to circulate the report.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p406/r4.anchor: وأقول : ما كان لابن عمرو في سيفيه ، ومقاتلته بهما علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r1.claim: One view refers to the skies and earth of this world, with the exception allowing an added duration of the bliss beyond them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r1.anchor: دامت سموات الدنيا وأرضها إلا ما شاء ربك من الزيادة عليها في الخلود فيها

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r2.claim: A second view takes the exception as the duration of the Resurrection Day.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r2.anchor: إلا ما شاء ربك من مدة يوم القيامة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says it allows the time spent in the Fire until they are brought out of it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r3.anchor: من مدة مكثهم في النار إلى أن يخرجوا منها , قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r4.claim: A fourth view identifies those blessed as monotheists and the exception as polytheists, resembling Abu Nadra's view.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r4.anchor: يعني أهل الشرك , وهو يشبه قول أبي نضرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r5.claim: A fifth view makes illā mean 'and,' so the phrase continues with the unending gift; the cited couplet illustrates this usage.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r5.anchor: فتكون { إلا } هنا بمعنى الواو كقول الشاعر : وكل أخ مفارقه أخوه

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r6.claim: One gloss takes ghayr majdhūdh as uncut or uninterrupted.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p506#2/r7.claim: A second gloss takes it as not withheld.

MUJAHID:v1p308#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p308#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p308#4/r1.claim: Ghayr majdhudh means uncut or uninterrupted.
MUJAHID:v1p308#4/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ عطاء غير مجذوذ ﴾ يعني مقطوع

MUQATIL:11:108/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:108/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:108/r1.claim: As the heavens and earth endure for worldly people, the happy remain in Paradise and do not leave it.
MUQATIL:11:108/r1.anchor: ثم لا يخرجون منها، وكذلك السعداء في الجنة

MUQATIL:11:108/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:108/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:108/r2.claim: Here the exception means monotheists whom God brings out of the Fire.
MUQATIL:11:108/r2.anchor: يعني الموحدين الذين يخرجون من النار

MUQATIL:11:108/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:108/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:108/r3.claim: The gift is never cut off from them.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r1.claim: Ḥamza, ʿAlī, and Ḥafṣ read saʿidū with saʿida as an intransitive form; saʿadahu yasʿaduhu is transitive.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r1.anchor: سعدوا حمزة وعلى وحفص سعد لازم وسعده يسعده متعد

NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r2.claim: One explanation makes the exception refer to what is greater than Paradise's bliss: seeing God and His good pleasure.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r2.anchor: وذلك أن لهم سوى الجنة ما هو اكبر منها وهو رؤية الله تعالى ورضوانه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r3.claim: Alternatively, God may punish a sinner for the measure of his sin before admitting him to Paradise.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r3.anchor: أو معناهاإلا من شاء أن يعذبه بقدر ذنبه قبل أن يدخله الجنة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r4.claim: Abū Hurayra reports from the Prophet that the exception in both verses concerns Paradise's people: sinful Muslims do not remain eternally in Hell, and do not remain eternally in Paradise without having entered it.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r4.anchor: عن أبى هريرة رضى الله عنه عن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال الاستثناء فى الآيتين لأهل الجنة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r5.claim: The Muʿtazila reject the transmitted reports because they deny that sinners leave Hell; the author calls this a manifest sin.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r5.anchor: والمعتزلة لما لم يروا خروج العصاة من النار ردوا الأحاديث المروية فى هذا الباب وكفى به اثما مبينا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r6.claim: The gift is not cut off but continues without end, as with the unending reward in 41:8.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r6.anchor: غير مقطوع ولكنه ممتد إلى غير نهاية كقوله لهم أجر غير ممنون

NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r7.claim: ʿAṭāʾan is an accusative verbal noun, meaning that they were given a gift.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r7.anchor: وهو نصب فى المصدر أى اعطوا عطاء

NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r8.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r8.claim: A report says the Jahmiyya disbelieved four verses: the enduring fruit, God's enduring bounty, and provision that is neither cut off nor withheld, alongside this verse.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p173/r8.anchor: قيل كفرت الجهمية بأربع آيات عطاء غير مجذوذ أكلها دائم وما عند الله باق

QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج عن أهل المعاني
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#2/r1.claim: One interpretation places the exception in the interval before final abode: time at graves, judgment, earthly life, the barzakh, and standing for the reckoning.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#2/r1.anchor: فأحد القولين: «خالدين فيها ما دامت السموات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك» من مقدار موقفهم على رأس قبورهم

QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج عن أهل المعاني
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#2/r2.claim: Another interpretation makes the exception an increase beyond the stated duration: increased bliss for Paradise’s people and increased punishment for Hell’s people.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#2/r2.anchor: والقول الآخر: وقوع الاستثناء في الزيادة على النعيم والعذاب، وتقديره: «خالدين فيها ما دامت السموات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك»

QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#2/r3.speaker: الترمذي الحكيم أبو عبد الله محمد بن علي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#2/r3.claim: Al-Tirmidhī al-Ḥakīm prefers the increase interpretation: the stated duration is the world’s term, followed by an unbounded increase in both abodes; the author explains that the covenant transaction ends, then the final outcome depends on whether one meets God affirming His oneness or associating partners.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#2/r3.anchor: واختاره الترمذي الحكيم أبو عبد الله محمد بن علي، أي خالدين فيها مقدار دوام السموات والأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#3/r1.claim: Qurʾān 2:150 is cited as an example where illā is read with the sense “and not those who wronged.”
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#3/r1.anchor: إلا الذين ظلموا [البقرة: 150] أي ولا الذين ظلموا

QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#3/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#3/r2.claim: Another view takes illā to mean “as”: the phrase means as God wills, like the usage in 4:22.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#3/r2.anchor: وقيل: معناه كما شاء ربك كقوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#3/r3.claim: The exception can be a conventional qualification of a settled promise, like the promise of secure entry to the Sacred Mosque; it is neither a connected nor disconnected exception and does not imply uncertainty, since the decree is fixed. “A gift uncut off” supports this.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#3/r3.anchor: العاشر وهو أن قوله تعالى: «إلا ما شاء ربك» إنما ذلك على طريق الاستثناء الذي ندب الشرع إلى استعماله

QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#3/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#3/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says God’s decree of eternal residence was already settled, so the exception follows an already decisive decree, as in the promise of entry to the Sacred Mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:107-108#3/r4.anchor: ونحوه عن أبي عبيد قال: تقدمت عزيمة المشيئة من الله تعالى في خلود الفريقين في الدارين

QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r1.claim: An eleventh view makes the wretched who leave Hell believers from Muḥammad’s community, and the blessed who first enter Hell sinners later admitted to Paradise; “what” means “who.”
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r1.anchor: وقول حادي عشر وهو أن الأشقياء هم السعداء، والسعداء هم الأشقياء لا غيرهم

QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports Ibn ʿAbbās explaining that they are wretched when they enter the Fire, then fortunate when they leave it and enter Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r2.anchor: كما روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس إذ قال: الذين سعدوا شقوا بدخول النار ثم سعدوا بالخروج منها

QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r3.speaker: الأعمش وحفص وحمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r3.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read saʿidū with ḍamma on the sīn.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r3.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وحفص وحمزة والكسائي «وأما الذين سعدوا» بضم السين

QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr argues for this vocalization because the preceding form is shaqū, not ashqaw.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: والدليل على أنه سعدوا أن الأول شقوا ولم يقل أشقوا

QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r5.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r5.claim: Al-Naḥḥās quotes ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān’s objection that al-Kisāʾī’s reading is ungrammatical: Arabic says saʿida and asʿada, not saʿadahu; masʿūd can be explained as shortening makān masʿūd fīhi.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r5.anchor: قال النحاس: ورأيت علي بن سليمان يتعجب من قراءة الكسائي «سعدوا» مع علمه بالعربية

QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r6.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r6.claim: Al-Mahdawī says the ḍamma reading is analogized to masʿūd but is rare and irregular, because Arabic says asʿadahu, not saʿadahu.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r7.speaker: الثعلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r7.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī explains the ḍamma form as “they were granted felicity” and says saʿida and asʿada have the same meaning.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r8.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r8.claim: The other readers use fatḥa on the sīn by analogy with shaqū; Abū ʿUbayd and Abū Ḥātim prefer this reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r8.anchor: وقرأ الباقون «سعدوا» بفتح السين قياسا على «شقوا» واختاره أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم

QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r9.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r9.claim: Al-Jawharī says happiness is the opposite of wretchedness; saʿida is parallel to salima, and saʿida/masʿūd are used rather than masʿad.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r9.anchor: وقال الجوهري: والسعادة خلاف الشقاوة تقول: منه سعد الرجل بالكسر فهو سعيد، مثل سلم فهو سليم

QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r10.speaker: القشيري أبو نصر عبد الرحيم
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r10.claim: Al-Qushayrī cites both saʿadahu Allāh and asʿadahu Allāh as valid, supporting the Kufan position.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108/r10.anchor: وقال القشيري أبو نصر عبد الرحيم: وقد ورد سعده الله فهو مسعود، وأسعده الله فهو مسعد

QURTUBI-FULL:11:108-109/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108-109/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108-109/r1.claim: Ghayr majdhūdh means not cut off; jadhdh means to cut, and al-Nābigha’s verse uses it of cutting the layered armor.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108-109/r1.anchor: أي غير مقطوع من جذّه يجذه أي قطعه قال النابغة:

QURTUBI-FULL:11:108-109/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108-109/r2.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108-109/r2.claim: Sībawayh says saʿida fulān is not used, just as shaqiya fulān is not used, because the verb is intransitive.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:108-109/r2.anchor: وقال سيبويه: لا يقال سعد فلان كما لا يقال شقي فلان

QASHANI:11:105-108/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:105-108/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:105-108/r2.claim: Fire signifies the self’s punishment through deprivation and painful states; the garden signifies its reward through attaining desires and pleasures.
QASHANI:11:105-108/r2.anchor: المراد بالنار والجنة عذاب النفس بنار الحرمان عن المراد وآلام الهيئات والآثار وثواب النفس بجنة حصول المرادات واللذات

QASHANI:11:105-108/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:105-108/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:105-108/r3.claim: On the outwardly careful reading, the wretched leave that fire only for worse fires of the heart and spirit, while the blessed move to greater gardens of the heart’s divine disclosure and the spirit’s encounter with God.
QASHANI:11:105-108/r3.anchor: خروج الشقي منها إلى ما هو أشد منه من نيران القلب

QASHANI:11:105-108/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:105-108/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:105-108/r4.claim: The blessed cannot leave paradise for fire; the unsevered gift supports the permanence of their state and, by opposition, the permanence of the wretched person’s punishment, while the threat in 11:107 is severe.
QASHANI:11:105-108/r4.anchor: لكون الشقي في مقابلة السعيد وخروج السعيد من الجنة إلى النار محال

QASHANI:11:105-108/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:105-108/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:105-108/r8.claim: The blessed traverse the gardens, then the exception refers to their annihilation in the oneness of essence and the ecstasy of love; in selfless witnessing, no separate spirit or other remains, beyond all imaginable description.
QASHANI:11:105-108/r8.anchor: فهو بفنائه في أحدية الذات واحتراقه بلوعة العشق في سبحات الجمال

RAZI-FULL:v18p51/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p51/r1.speaker: قائل
RAZI-FULL:v18p51/r1.claim: An analogy about permanence helps only if the comparison case is known; the afterlife heavens and their endless duration are not known to most people, making the comparison uninformative.
RAZI-FULL:v18p51/r1.anchor: ولقائل أن يقول : التشبيه إنما يحسن ويجوز إذا كان حال المشبه به معلوما مقررا

RAZI-FULL:v18p51/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p51/r2.speaker: قالوا
RAZI-FULL:v18p51/r2.claim: Arab idiom uses the duration of heaven and earth, night and day, seas, or mountains to mean endless permanence, and the Qur'an addresses Arabs in their idiom.
RAZI-FULL:v18p51/r2.anchor: الوجه الثاني : في الجواب قالوا إن العرب يعبرون عن الدوام والأبد بقولهم

RAZI-FULL:v18p51/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p51/r3.speaker: قائل
RAZI-FULL:v18p51/r3.claim: If the phrase bars punishment from continuing after the heavens end, it entails punishment's termination; if it does not, the idiom reply was unnecessary, so that reply fails either way.
RAZI-FULL:v18p51/r3.anchor: ولقائل أن يقول : هل تسلمون أن قول القائل : خالدين فيها ما دامت السموات

RAZI-FULL:v18p52/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p52/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p52/r1.claim: The verse affirms that their punishment lasts whenever the heavens and earth last; denying that condition does not prove punishment ends, just as denying someone is human does not prove they are not an animal.
RAZI-FULL:v18p52/r1.anchor: واعلم أن الجواب الحق عندي في هذا الباب شيء آخر ، وهو أن المعهود من الآية أنه متى كانت السموات

RAZI-FULL:v18p52/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p52/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p52/r2.claim: The comparison still benefits readers by conveying an immense duration beyond the mind's grasp; whether that duration has an end is established by other proofs.
RAZI-FULL:v18p52/r2.anchor: قلنا بل فيه أعظم الفوائد وهو أنه يدل على نفاذ ذلك العذاب دهرا دهرا ، وزمانا لا يحيط العقل

RAZI-FULL:v18p52/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p52/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة وابن الأنباري والفراء
RAZI-FULL:v18p52/r3.claim: They treat the exception as a disclaimer God will never enact, like a speaker vowing to strike someone unless he sees otherwise while still intending to strike.
RAZI-FULL:v18p52/r3.anchor: وهو الذي ذكره ابن قتيبة وابن الأنباري والفراء

RAZI-FULL:v18p52/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p52/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p52/r4.claim: Razi rejects the disclaimer analogy: the verse states an exception for a period God willed, so the wording entails that this will occurred, unlike the merely hypothetical change of mind in the example.
RAZI-FULL:v18p52/r4.anchor: هذا ضعيف لأنه إذا قال : لأضربنك إلا أن أرى غير ذلك ، معناه

RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r1.claim: A proposed reading takes illa as 'beyond': the phrase first names the longest span Arabs knew, then adds duration without end as an increase beyond it.
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r1.anchor: الوجه الثاني : في الجواب أن يقال

RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r2.claim: One proposal excludes the time the damned stand for judgment, when they are not yet in Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r2.anchor: الوجه الثالث : في الجواب وهو أن المراد من هذا الاستثناء زمان وقوفهم في الموقف

RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r3.speaker: أبو بكر الأصم
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r3.claim: Al-Asamm says the exception may be their time in the grave or, alternatively, the duration of their worldly lives; afterward they enter Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r3.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الأصم المراد إلا ما شاء ربك وهو حال كونهم في القبر

RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r4.claim: Another proposal attaches the exception to their sighing and gasping: once they become motionless, that combined condition ceases even though they remain in Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r4.anchor: الوجه الرابع : في الجواب قالوا : الاستثناء يرجع إلى قوله

RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r5.claim: A further proposal says the damned may be moved out of the fire into extreme cold or other forms of torment, making the exception refer to their time outside the fire.
RAZI-FULL:v18p53/r5.anchor: الوجه الخامس : في الجواب أن يحمل هذا الاستثناء على أن أهل العذاب

RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r2.speaker: قائل
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r2.claim: An objection asks whether this reading works only after the other explanations fail and notes that an exception also appears for the blessed.
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r2.anchor: فإن قيل : فهذا الوجه إنما يتعين إذا فسدت سائر الوجوه

RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r3.claim: Razi rejects reading illa as 'beyond' because it departs from the apparent sense of the exception.
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r3.anchor: أما حمل كلمة ( إلا ) على سوى فهو عدول عن الظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r4.claim: He rejects exclusions for worldly life, the grave, or judgment: the exception concerns everlasting residence in Hell, which cannot exist before entry into Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r4.anchor: عن الخلود في النار ، ومن المعلوم أن الخلود في النار

RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r5.claim: He rejects attaching the exception to sighing and gasping as another departure from the apparent meaning.

RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r6.claim: He rejects transfer to extreme cold as the exception: authentic reports say people move between fire and cold repeatedly each day, not only after the heavens' duration ends.
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r6.anchor: والأخبار الصحيحة دلت على أن النقل من النار إلى الزمهرير وبالعكس يحصل في كل يوم مرارا

RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r7.claim: The community agrees that nobody enters Paradise and later leaves for Hell, so the exception for the blessed needs interpretation; no such consensus constrains the apparent reading for the damned.
RAZI-FULL:v18p53#2/r7.anchor: أجمعت الأمة على أنه يمتنع أن يقال : إن أحدا يدخل الجنة ثم يخرج منها إلى النار

RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r1.claim: If the exception removes sinful believers from Hell, the verse's assertion that God does what He wills fittingly joins His display of power with mercy: no one has a claim over Him.
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r1.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى لما ذكر هذا الاستثناء قال : { إن ربك فعال لما يريد } وهذا يحسن انطباقه

RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r2.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from Asim read saʿidū with ḍamma on the sīn; the other readers use fatḥa. The ḍamma reflects dropping the augment from asʿada; saʿida and asʿada have the same sense.
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r2.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم { سعدوا } بضم السين والباقون بفتحها

RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r3.claim: The ḍamma reading is possible by removing the added form from asʿada; saʿida is intransitive while asʿada is transitive, though both mean the same, as reflected in the name al-Masʿūd.
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r3.anchor: وإنما جاز ضم السين لأنه على حذف الزيادة من أسعد ولأن سعد لا يتعدى وأسعد يتعدى وسعد وأسعد بمعنى

RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r4.claim: For the blessed, Razi adds that some may be raised from Paradise to the Throne or to exalted stations known only to God.
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r4.anchor: وههنا وجه آخر وهو أنه ربما اتفق لبعضهم أن يرفع من الجنة إلى العرش

RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r5.claim: The root jadhdha means to cut, so God's gift described as ghayr majdhūdh is uncut or uninterrupted; compare the Garden's bounty as 'neither cut off nor withheld.'
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r5.anchor: جذه يجذه جذا إذا قطعه وجذ الله دابرهم ، فقوله : { غير مجذوذ } أي غير مقطوع

RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r6.claim: Because the blessed are explicitly told that their gift is not cut off while the damned receive no such clarification, Razi infers that their exception means termination.
RAZI-FULL:v18p54/r6.anchor: فلما خص هذا الموضع بهذا البيان ولم يذكر ذلك في جانب الأشقياء دل ذلك على أن المراد من ذلك الاستثناء هو الانقطاع

QUSHAYRI:v2p59/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p59/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p59/r1.claim: The blessed enjoy nearness in this world and reward in the next; unbelievers face separation now and burning later.
QUSHAYRI:v2p59/r1.anchor: لهم اليوم جناب القربة ، ولهم غدا جناب المثوبة . والكفار اليوم في عقوبة الفرقة ، وغدا في عقوبة الحرقة

QUSHAYRI:v2p59/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p59/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p59/r2.claim: One reading of God’s will allows no interval of the people of Paradise’s time, before or after entry, to be excluded from their happiness.
QUSHAYRI:v2p59/r2.anchor: { فعال لما يريد } فلا استثناء لبعض أوقات أهل الجنة من أول أمرهم قبل دخولهم الجنة أو بعده

QUSHAYRI:v2p59/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p59/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p59/r3.claim: Another possibility is that their blessed duration extends beyond the time of the heavens and earth.
QUSHAYRI:v2p59/r3.anchor: أو يحتمل أنه يزيد على مدة السموات والأرض

QUSHAYRI:v2p59/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p59/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p59/r4.claim: The phrase means an unsevered gift and proves that Paradise’s blessings are neither cut off nor withheld.
QUSHAYRI:v2p59/r4.anchor: وفي قوله { عطآء غير مجذوذ } - أي عطاء غير مقطوع - دليل على أن تلك النعم غير مقطوعة ولا ممنوعة

STUDYQURAN:11:106/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:106/r2.speaker: al-Bayḍāwī
STUDYQURAN:11:106/r2.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī says the heavens and earth enduring refers to the Afterlife's basic topographic setting, not serial time or physical-world time; 14:48 depicts the earth and heavens changed on that Day.
STUDYQURAN:11:106/r2.anchor: Bayḍāwī argues that the period in Hell described as for so long as

STUDYQURAN:11:106/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:106/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:106/r3.claim: The Garden's unending gift means that it will never cease.
STUDYQURAN:11:106/r3.anchor: with the added nuance that it is a gift unfailing, which is interpreted to mean that the Garden will never cease (Kl).

TAB-FULL:v12p582/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p582/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v12p582/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says God explains His will for Paradise's people as an unending gift, but does not state what He wills for Hell's people; it could extend or shorten their stay.

TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r1.speaker: جماعة من قراء الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r1.claim: A group of Kufan reciters read “suʿidū” with ḍamma on the sīn, meaning they were granted felicity.
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r1.anchor: جماعة من قراء الكوفة: {وأما الذين سعدوا} [هود: 108] بضم السين

TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī accepts both readings as established and correct.
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r2.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أنهما قراءتان معروفتان، فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فمصيب الصواب.

TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r3.claim: Although Arabic normally says God made someone happy with “asʿadahu,” passive forms such as “majnūn” and “maḥbūb” can take this pattern; when naming the agent, Arabs say “ajannahu” and “aḥabbahu.”
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r3.anchor: قيل: ذلك نظير قولهم: هو مجنون محبوب فيما لم يسم فاعله، فإذا سموا فاعله، قيل: أجنه الله وأحبه

TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r4.claim: The happy are in Paradise by God's mercy, remaining there as long as the heavens and earth endure, meaning forever, except as their Lord wills.
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r4.anchor: وتأويل ذلك: وأما الذين سعدوا برحمة الله، فهم في الجنة خالدين فيها ما دامت السموات والأرض، يقول: أبدا، إلا ما شاء ربك.

TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the exception is the period believers who leave Hell spend there before entering Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: " {وأما الذين سعدوا

TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r6.speaker: أبو سنان
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r6.claim: Abū Sinān says God's will is that they remain in Paradise forever, as confirmed by the following phrase, “an unending gift.”
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي مالك، يعني ثعلبة، عن أبي سنان، " {وأما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة خالدين فيها ما دامت السموات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك} قال: ومشيئته خلودهم فيها

TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r7.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r7.claim: One Arabic grammatical explanation treats the exception as stated but never enacted, like promising to strike someone unless one sees otherwise while being resolved to strike.
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r7.anchor: فقال بعضهم في ذلك معنيان: أحدهما أن تجعله استثناء يستثنيه ولا يفعله، كقولك: والله لأضربنك إلا أن أرى غير ذلك

TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r8.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r8.claim: Another grammatical explanation uses “illā” in the sense of “siwā” (“besides”), so the exception adds to the everlasting duration.
TAB-FULL:v12p584#2/r8.anchor: والقول الآخر: أن العرب إذا استثنت شيئا كثيرا مع مثله، ومع ما هو أكثر منه كان معنى إلا ومعنى الواو «سوى»

TAB-FULL:v12p587/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r1.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r1.claim: The “besides” reading means an addition to their endless duration; the grammarian prefers it because God does not break His promise, and “an unending gift” shows the exception does not cut them off.
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r1.anchor: ما زادهم من الخلود والأبد. ومثله في الكلام أن تقول: لي عليك ألف إلا الألفين اللذين قبله.

TAB-FULL:v12p587/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r2.speaker: آخر من أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r2.claim: A third grammatical possibility is that the exception is the believers' exclusion from Paradise between death and resurrection in the barzakh; afterward their stay is eternal.
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r2.anchor: وقال آخر منهم بنحو هذا القول، وقالوا: جائز فيه وجه ثالث، وهو أن يكون استثني من خلودهم في الجنة احتباسهم عنها ما بين الموت والبعث

TAB-FULL:v12p587/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r3.speaker: آخر من أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r3.claim: A further possibility takes the duration idiom as “forever” and excludes their prior earthly lives, when they were not yet in Paradise or Hell.
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r3.anchor: وقال آخر منهم: جائز أن يكون دوام السموات والأرض بمعنى الأبد على ما تعرف العرب وتستعمل، وتستثني المشيئة من دوامها

TAB-FULL:v12p587/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers al-Ḍaḥḥāk's interpretation: the exception is the believers' time in Hell before entry to Paradise. Arabic “illā” most commonly marks a real exception, and nothing here indicates a different sense, so the verse is particular in scope.
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r4.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك عندي بالصواب، القول الذي ذكرته عن الضحاك،

TAB-FULL:v12p587/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r5.claim: “An unsevered gift” means a gift from God that is not cut off; the root phrase “jadhadhtu al-shayʾ” means “I cut the thing.”
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r5.anchor: وأما قوله: {عطاء غير مجذوذ} [هود: 108] فإنه يعني عطاء من الله غير مقطوع عنهم، من قولهم: جذذت الشيء أجذه جذا: إذا قطعته، كما قال النابغة

TAB-FULL:v12p587/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r6.claim: Al-Nābigha's poem uses “tajudhdhu” to mean “cut,” supporting the gloss of “majdhūdh.”
TAB-FULL:v12p587/r6.anchor: كما قال النابغة: [البحر الطويل] تجذ السلوقي المضاعف نسجه … ويوقدن بالصفاح نار الحباحب

TAB-FULL:v12p589/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the gift is not cut off.
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك، " {عطاء غير مجذوذ} [هود: 108] قال: غير مقطوع "

TAB-FULL:v12p589/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r2.claim: Qatāda says the gift is uninterrupted.
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {عطاء غير مجذوذ} [هود: 108] يقول: غير منقطع "

TAB-FULL:v12p589/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the gift is not cut off.
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، " {عطاء غير مجذوذ} [هود: 108] يقول: عطاء غير مقطوع "

TAB-FULL:v12p589/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r5.claim: In another transmission, Mujāhid glosses the complete phrase as “not cut off.”
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: " {عطاء غير مجذوذ} [هود: 108] قال: غير مقطوع "

TAB-FULL:v12p589/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r6.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says this gift has been made certain and is uninterrupted.
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r6.anchor: عن أبي العالية، " قوله: {عطاء غير مجذوذ} [هود: 108] قال: أما هذه فقد أمضاها، يقول: عطاء غير منقطع "

TAB-FULL:v12p589/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r7.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas transmits the same gloss from Abū al-ʿĀliya: the gift is uninterrupted.
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r7.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس، عن أبي العالية، " قوله: {عطاء غير مجذوذ} [هود: 108] قال: أما هذه فقد أمضاها

TAB-FULL:v12p589/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says the gift is not taken away from them.
TAB-FULL:v12p589/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {عطاء غير مجذوذ} [هود: 108] غير منزوع منهم

TABATABAI:11:100-108/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r2.claim: The questioning and intermediate reward or punishment in individual graves differ from the final accounting and decisive, everlasting reward of the Resurrection; barzakh questioning completes the record for Judgment Day, while its garden or fire is only a preliminary lodging.
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r2.anchor: فإن الذي يستقبل الإنسان في البرزخ هو المسألة لتكميل صحيفة أعماله ليدخر لفصل القضاء يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:11:100-108/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r4.claim: The slain are described as alive and enjoying provision in the grave, but the passage does not mention a final reckoning or the eternal Garden; the dead remain in barzakh until resurrection, between worldly life and the true afterlife.
TABATABAI:11:100-108/r4.anchor: فالآية صريحة في عالم القبر ولم تذكر حسابا ولا جنة الخلد وإنما ذكرت شيئا من التنعم إجمالا

TABATABAI:11:106-108/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r6.claim: The clause describes the duration of Hell's inhabitants, just as the next verse describes the Garden's inhabitants, confirming their settled residence.
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r6.anchor: بيان لمكث أهل النار فيها كما أن الآية التالية

TABATABAI:11:106-108/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r7.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r7.claim: Al-Rāghib defines khulūd as remaining unchanged and free from corruption; Arabs use it for things lasting a long time, even if mortal, then by extension for permanence.
TABATABAI:11:106-108/r7.anchor: قال الراغب في المفردات الخلود هو تبري الشيء من اعتراض الفساد وبقاؤه على الحالة التي هو عليها

TABATABAI:11:107-108/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:107-108/r4.claim: The phrase reinforces permanence, yet worldly heavens and earth end while the Garden and Fire last forever; it also seems to measure post-Resurrection residence by a world that ends before it begins, the harder problem.
TABATABAI:11:107-108/r4.anchor: وعلى هذا يشكل الأمر في الآيتين من جهتين إحداهما تحديد الخلود المؤبد بمدة دوام السماوات والأرض

TABATABAI:11:107-108/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:107-108/r5.claim: The answer begins from Qur'anic mention of an afterlife earth and heavens unlike those of this world, removing the apparent time limit on everlasting residence.
TABATABAI:11:107-108/r5.anchor: والذي يحسم الإشكال أنه تعالى يذكر في كلامه أن في الآخرة أرضا وسماوات وإن كانت غير ما في الدنيا بوجه

TABATABAI:11:100-108#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#6/r1.claim: The Qur'an describes an afterlife earth and heavens, the Garden's inhabitants inheriting the earth, and the righteous receiving the final home; all that is with God endures, so only this world's heavens and earth perish while the afterlife's persist.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#6/r1.anchor: فللآخرة سماوات وأرض كما أن فيها جنة ونارا ولهما أهلا

TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that the afterlife has heavens and earth, citing the earth's replacement and the Garden's inhabitants inheriting the earth.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r1.anchor: حيث قال والدليل على أن لها سماوات وأرضا

TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also suggests that what supports and shades the Garden and Fire counts as their earth and heaven, whether a created sky or the Throne.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r2.anchor: ولأنه لا بد لأرض الآخرة مما تقلهم وتظلهم إما سماء يخلقها الله تعالى أو يظلهم العرش

TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the support-and-shade argument as weak: it makes heavens and earth dependent on the Garden and Fire, reverses the verse's duration relation, and fails to explain plural heavens.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r3.anchor: وإن كان الوجه الذي أشار إليه ثانيا سخيفا لأنه إثبات للسماء والأرض من جهة الإضافة

TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r4.speaker: القاضي
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī objects that comparing Paradise and Hell's duration to afterlife heavens and earth cannot clarify the point for most people, who do not know those things endure.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r4.anchor: حيث قال وفيه نظر لأنه تشبيه بما لا يعرف أكثر الخلق وجوده ودوامه

TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r5.claim: The author answers that God's speech reveals the eternity of both the afterlife and its heavens and earth, so one revealed truth may explain the duration of another even if one is less familiar.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r5.anchor: وجوابه أنا إنما عرفنا دوام الجنة والنار بأهلهما من كلامه تعالى كما عرفنا وجود سماوات وأرض لهما

TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r6.speaker: الآلوسي
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the apparent sense is the familiar celestial bodies and recommends another explanation.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r6.anchor: أن المتبادر من السماوات والأرض هذه الأجرام المعهودة عندنا فالأولى أن يلتمس هناك وجه آخر

TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#7/r7.claim: The author replies that language gives general concepts, while reflection and cross-reading determine their intended referents; the Qur'an interprets and confirms itself, so familiar worldly referents need not be imposed.

TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r1.claim: The second view means the heavens and earth of Paradise and Hell: what is above and shades them is heaven, and what they rest on is earth.
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r1.anchor: الوجه الثاني إن المراد سماوات الجنة والنار وأرضهما أي ما يظلهما وما يقلهما

TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r2.claim: The author rejects that view because it does not explain why the verse uses plural heavens, and he has already shown its broader conceptual problem.
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r2.anchor: على أن هذا الوجه لا يفي لبيان السبب في إيراد السماوات في الآية بلفظ الجمع

TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r3.speaker: مفسرون
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r3.claim: A third view takes the phrase as a comparison: Paradise and Hell last as long as the afterlife, just as the worldly heavens and earth last for their own span.
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r3.anchor: الوجه الثالث إن المراد ما دامت الآخرة وهي دائمة أبدا كما أن دوام السماء والأرض في الدنيا قدر مدة بقائها

TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r4.claim: If read as a simile, this third view implies termination contrary to the intended meaning; any other reading is unsupported by the wording.
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r4.anchor: وفيه إنه لو أريد بذلك التشبيه كما ذكرناه أفاد خلاف المقصود أعني الانقطاع

TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r5.speaker: مفسرون
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r5.claim: A fourth view treats the phrase as Arabic hyperbole for endless duration, like expressions that last as long as night and day differ or stars rise.
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r5.anchor: الوجه الرابع إن المراد به التبعيد وإفادة الأبدية لا أن المراد به التحديد بمدة بقاء السماوات والأرض بعينها

TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r6.claim: The author rejects this usage for God, who explicitly teaches that the heavens and earth are appointed and perishable; their names cannot properly be used as a term for eternity in His speech.
TABATABAI:11:107-108#2/r6.anchor: وأما من يصرح في كلامه بأنها مؤجلة الوجود منقطعة فانية ويعد الإيمان بذلك إحدى فرائض النفوس

TABATABAI:11:107-108#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108#3/r1.speaker: مفسرون
TABATABAI:11:107-108#3/r1.claim: A fifth view gives the damned a finite span as long as the heavens and earth last, then an added endless duration, analogously to people remaining for epochs in 78:23.
TABATABAI:11:107-108#3/r1.anchor: الوجه الخامس أن يكون المراد أنهم خالدون بمدة بقاء السماوات والأرض التي يعلم انقطاعها ثم يزيدهم الله سبحانه على ذلك

TABATABAI:11:107-108#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:107-108#3/r2.claim: The author rejects the fifth view because it assumes the phrase divides duration into a finite part and an infinite addition, a reading requiring unstated premises absent from the wording.
TABATABAI:11:107-108#3/r2.anchor: وفيه إنه على الظاهر مبني على استفادة بعض المدة

TABATABAI:11:107-108#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108#3/r3.speaker: مفسرون
TABATABAI:11:107-108#3/r3.claim: A sixth view identifies the Garden and Fire here with their Barzakh counterparts, which last until Resurrection, when their inhabitants leave for judgment.
TABATABAI:11:107-108#3/r3.anchor: الوجه السادس إن المراد بالنار والجنة نار البرزخ وجنتها وهما خالدتان ما دامت السماوات والأرض

TABATABAI:11:107-108#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:107-108#3/r4.claim: The author rejects the Barzakh view as contrary to the context, which describes Resurrection Day and its eternal reward and punishment; Barzakh punishment is exposure to the Fire, not entry into it.
TABATABAI:11:107-108#3/r4.anchor: على أن الله سبحانه يذكر عذاب أهل البرزخ بالعرض على النار لا بدخول النار

TABATABAI:11:107-108#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108#4/r1.speaker: مفسرون
TABATABAI:11:107-108#4/r1.claim: A seventh view reads entering Hell as entering Satan's authority, whose form becomes Fire, and dwelling in the Garden as God's authority, whose form becomes bliss; people may enter or leave either through changes in faith and conduct.
TABATABAI:11:107-108#4/r1.anchor: الوجه السابع إن المراد بدخول النار الدخول في ولاية الشيطان وبالكون في الجنة الكون في ولاية الله

TABATABAI:11:107-108#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:107-108#4/r2.claim: The author says this is sound as an inward meaning but not the apparent one: the passage describes Resurrection's unique terrors to warn and reassure, not pre-Resurrection spiritual states hidden from its audience.
TABATABAI:11:107-108#4/r2.anchor: نعم هو معنى صحيح في نفسه في باطن القرآن

TABATABAI:11:107-108#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108#6/r5.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:11:107-108#6/r5.claim: A fourth view attaches the Hell exception to kinds of torment beyond sighing and gasping, and the Garden exception to kinds of pleasure, inferred from its uncut gift.
TABATABAI:11:107-108#6/r5.anchor: ورابعها إن الاستثناء الأول متصل بقوله

TABATABAI:11:107-108#6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108#6/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:107-108#6/r6.claim: The author rejects the fourth view as an unsupported break in parallel context: 'uncut gift' establishes duration, not kinds of pleasure, and there is no cue for the proposed exception.
TABATABAI:11:107-108#6/r6.anchor: وفيه إنه قطع لاتصال السياق ووحدته من غير دليل

TABATABAI:11:107-108#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108#5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:107-108#5/r6.claim: Because the Garden is an uncut gift, its exception signals God's continuing ability to expel its inhabitants, not an actual exit; He will not do so, keeping His promise and retaining unrestricted power and sovereignty.
TABATABAI:11:107-108#5/r6.anchor: ولازمه أن لا يكون الاستثناء مشيرا إلى تحقق الوقوع فإنه لا يلائم كون الجنة عطاء غير مقطوع

TABATABAI:11:107-108#5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:107-108#5/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:107-108#5/r7.claim: The paired exceptions preserve God's absolute power: no gift or withholding binds Him or removes His ability to act otherwise; the Hell clause matches the Garden clause, and reports of some sinners leaving Hell remain compatible.
TABATABAI:11:107-108#5/r7.anchor: فأهل الخلود في النار كأهل الخلود في الجنة لا يخرجون منها أبدا إلا أن يشاء الله سبحانه ذلك لأنه على كل شيء قدير

TABATABAI:11:108/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108/r1.claim: A fifth view takes illa as waw: they abide as long as heaven and earth and for whatever additional duration God wills.
TABATABAI:11:108/r1.anchor: أن " إلا " بمعنى الواو وإلا كان الكلام متناقضا والمعنى خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض وما شاء ربك من الزيادة على ذلك

TABATABAI:11:108/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this because illa meaning waw is unestablished; al-Farrāʾ mentions it, but scholars weakened it, and it also denies that the duration phrase implies permanence.

TABATABAI:11:108/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر بن عبد الله وأبو سعيد الخدري وجماعة من التابعين
TABATABAI:11:108/r3.claim: A sixth view identifies the wretched as sinful monotheists who enter Hell, then leave for Paradise; the exception covers their release and the happy group's prior time in Hell, so the same people are wretched there and happy in Paradise.
TABATABAI:11:108/r3.anchor: ونسبوا هذا القول إلى ابن عباس وجابر بن عبد الله وأبي سعيد الخدري من الصحابة وجماعة من التابعين

TABATABAI:11:108/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108/r4.claim: The context divides all people gathered for Judgment into two groups, and the clauses beginning with أما explain those same exhaustive groups; they cannot mean only selected sinners and former sinners.
TABATABAI:11:108/r4.anchor: مبدوين بأما التفصيلية مسوقان لتفصيل ما أجمل في قوله

TABATABAI:11:108/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108/r5.claim: Recasting the initial division as a special group leaves the general context unexplained and makes the doubled subjects, durations, and exceptions confusing and needlessly complex.
TABATABAI:11:108/r5.anchor: السياق الظاهر في وصف أهل الجمع عامة لا يساعد على إرادة طائفة خاصة منهم

TABATABAI:11:108#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī formulates the extraction view generally: all the gathered divide into Hell's wretched and Paradise's happy, while both exceptions concern sinful monotheists removed from Hell to Paradise; this avoids most earlier objections.
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r1.anchor: يمكن أن يقرر هذا الوجه على وجه التعميم بأن يقال المراد

TABATABAI:11:108#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r2.claim: A seventh view says the will clause reinforces endless abiding: God will never will their departure, so the exception does not shorten their stay; it protects permanence from any cause except God's will.
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r2.anchor: إن التعليق بالمشيئة إنما هو على سبيل التأكيد للخلود والتبعيد للخروج لأن الله سبحانه لا يشاء إلا خلودهم على ما حكم به

TABATABAI:11:108#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the seventh view lacks evidence that God will never will an end; the unsevered gift may suggest this for Paradise, but 11:107's statement that God does what He wills does not and may imply the opposite.
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r3.anchor: وهذا هو وجه الضعف فيه فإن قوله ولن يشاء أصلا.

TABATABAI:11:108#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r4.speaker: سلام بن المستنير البصري
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r4.claim: An eighth view makes the exception the time difference between successive groups entering Hell or Paradise, as groups are led in procession.
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r4.anchor: ونقل الوجه عن سلام بن المستنير البصري

TABATABAI:11:108#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r5.claim: The wording describes the duration of residence by its endpoint, not its start; everyone begins settling in Hell or Paradise on Judgment Day, so staggered arrivals do not explain the exception.
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r5.anchor: أن الوصف ناظر إلى مدة الكون في النار أو الجنة من جهة النهاية

TABATABAI:11:108#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر الطوسي
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r6.claim: A ninth view says the wretched remain in Hell during the world's duration, including their time in graves; when heaven and earth end, their torment pauses until resurrection, which is the exception.
TABATABAI:11:108#2/r6.anchor: نقله في مجمع البيان عن شيخنا أبي جعفر الطوسي في تفسيره ناقلا عن جمع من أصحابنا في تفاسيرهم

TABATABAI:11:108#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the ninth view restates the second view's reading of illa as 'other than' and inherits the objections raised against it.
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r1.anchor: وفيه إن مرجعه إلى الوجه الثاني المبني على أخذ

TABATABAI:11:108#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r2.speaker: أبو مجلز
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r2.claim: A tenth view makes the first exception exclude people God pardons before they enter Hell; the Paradise exception then excludes sinful monotheists who enter Hell and later reach Paradise.

TABATABAI:11:108#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r3.claim: The proposed account fits only the first exception and requires a different explanation for the second, breaking the two verses' contextual unity.
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r3.anchor: وفيه إن ما ذكره إنما يجري في أول الاستثناءين

TABATABAI:11:108#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r4.claim: People God pardons are not arbitrarily excused: pardon rests on a good deed or intercession, making them happy from the outset and included in Paradise's group, not wretches who must be excepted.
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r4.anchor: هم ليسوا بأشقياء حتى يستثنوا بل سعداء داخلون في الجنة من أول

TABATABAI:11:108#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r5.claim: The verse is read with سعدوا passive or active; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī prefers the active form because سعد is normally intransitive in Arabic usage.
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r5.anchor: قرئ سعدوا بالبناء للمجهول وبالبناء للمعلوم والثاني أوفق باللغة لأن مادة سعد لازمة في المعروف من استعمالهم

TABATABAI:11:108#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r6.claim: The passive reading subtly suggests that happiness and good come from God, whereas the evil attached to people comes from themselves, as 24:21 says.
TABATABAI:11:108#3/r6.anchor: لكن الأول وهو سعدوا بالبناء للمجهول مع كون

TABATABAI:11:108#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r2.claim: Jadh means cutting; ʿaṭāʾ ghayr majdūdh therefore means a gift that is not cut off.
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r2.anchor: والجذ هو القطع وعطاء غير مجذوذ أي غير مقطوع

TABATABAI:11:108#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r3.claim: Calling Paradise an unsevered gift despite the exception supports al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī's reading: the will clause affirms God's unrestricted power and continuing ownership of the matter.
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r3.anchor: وعده تعالى الجنة عطاء غير مجذوذ مع سبق الاستثناء من الخلود بقوله

TABATABAI:11:108#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r4.claim: Earlier interpretations based on moving people from Hell to Paradise cannot explain Paradise's exception: no one who enters the afterlife's Garden ever leaves it, as Quran and Sunna establish abundantly; Quranic evidence for some leaving Hell is less explicit.
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r4.anchor: من الجائز أن يخرج من نار الآخرة بعض من دخله لكن لا يخرج من جنة الآخرة وهي جنة الخلد أحد ممن دخلها جزاء أبدا

TABATABAI:11:108#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r5.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r5.claim: Majmaʿ al-Bayān reports community consensus that those deserving reward must enter Paradise and cannot leave after entry.
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r5.anchor: قال في مجمع البيان في وجوب دخول أهل الطاعة الجنة وعدم جواز خروجهم منها لإجماع الأمة على أن من استحق الثواب فلا بد أن يدخل الجنة

TABATABAI:11:108#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r6.claim: The duty to fulfill a promise follows a rational rule: withholding a promised right is injustice; punishment under a threat is God's own right, which He may enforce or waive, so He must reward the obedient but may forgive sinners.
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r6.anchor: قاعدة عقلية مسلمة وهي أن الوفاء بالوعد واجب دون الوفاء بالوعيد

TABATABAI:11:108#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r7.claim: The consensus about entry and permanence in Paradise is not independent proof; it rests on the Quran, Sunna, or reason accepted by the community.
TABATABAI:11:108#4/r7.anchor: والإجماع الذي ذكره مبني على الذي تسلموه من دلالة الكتاب والسنة أو العقل على ذلك

TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r1.claim: Jabir reports that after reciting the wretched people's passage through the exception, the Prophet said that if God wills to take some of them from Hell and put them in Paradise, He can.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r1.anchor: إن شاء الله أن يخرج أناسا من الذين شقوا من النار فيدخلهم الجنة فعل

TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r3.claim: Jahannamiyyun are a particular group of Hell's inhabitants: monotheists released through intercession, not all who enter Hell.
TABATABAI:11:100-108#11/r3.anchor: والمراد بالجهنميين طائفة خاصة من أهل النار وهم أهل التوحيد الخارجون منها بالشفاعة

TABATABAI:11:108#6/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r7.claim: Abu Basir reports Abu Jaʿfar's distinction: the exception is stated for Hell's people but, for Paradise's people, the clause is followed by 'an unsevered gift.'
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r7.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله

TABATABAI:11:108#6/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī explains that the Paradise exception, followed by an unsevered gift, does not remove anyone; it asserts unrestricted power, unlike Hell's exception followed by 'your Lord does what He wills,' which suggests an actual release.
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r8.anchor: يشير عليه السلام إلى أن الاستثناء بالمشيئة في أهل الجنة

TABATABAI:11:108#6/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r9.speaker: السدي
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r9.claim: Al-Suddi says both clauses were later abrogated: a Medinan threat removed hope that Hell's people would leave, while a promise to believers established Paradise's eternal duration.
TABATABAI:11:108#6/r9.anchor: أخرج أبو الشيخ عن السدي في قوله

TABATABAI:11:108#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects al-Suddi's abrogation claim: it assumes the verses imply eventual termination, lacks rational or transmitted basis, conflicts with explicit Paradise wording, and ignores other Meccan declarations of both groups' abiding.
TABATABAI:11:108#7/r1.anchor: ما ذكره من نسخ الآيتين زعما منه أنهما تدلان على الانقطاع

TABRISI:11:105/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105/r8.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر
TABRISI:11:105/r8.claim: Kūfan readers except Abū Bakr read سعدوا with ḍamma on the sīn; the rest read it with fatḥa.
TABRISI:11:105/r8.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر سعدوا بضم السين

TABRISI:11:105/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105/r9.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:11:105/r9.claim: Abū ʿAlī finds the ḍamma puzzling because سعد يسعد is intransitive like شقي; an exceptional dialect or paired intransitive/transitive pattern might explain it, while مسعود is not decisive evidence.
TABRISI:11:105/r9.anchor: حكى سيبويه سعد يسعد سعادة فهو سعيد

TABRISI:11:104-108/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:104-108/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:104-108/r1.claim: The cited لواقح is understood as ملاقح with an augment omitted; by analogy مسعود could derive from أسعد with its augment removed.
TABRISI:11:104-108/r1.anchor: يعني: ملاقح فجاء على حذف الزيادة

TABRISI:11:104-108/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:104-108/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:104-108/r2.claim: The poetic example يخرجن من أجواز ليل غاضي means مغض and illustrates deletion of an augment.

TABRISI:11:104-108/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:104-108/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:104-108/r3.claim: شقاء, شقاوة, and شقوة mean the same; the yāʾ in شقي comes from wāw, and saʿāda is the opposite of misery.
TABRISI:11:104-108/r3.anchor: الشقاء والشقاوة والشقوة بمعنى والياء في شقي

TABRISI:11:104-108/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:104-108/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:104-108/r7.claim: Khulūd and dawām both mean everlasting continuance; God is described as دائم but not as خالد.
TABRISI:11:104-108/r7.anchor: والخلود الكون في الأمر أبدا والدوام البقاء أبدا

TABRISI:11:104-108/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:104-108/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:104-108/r8.claim: Jadh means cutting off; the author gives Arabic usages including جذه and جذ الله دابرهم.
TABRISI:11:104-108/r8.anchor: والجذ القطع يقال جذه يجذه وجذ الله دابرهم

TABRISI:11:104-108/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:104-108/r9.speaker: النابغة
TABRISI:11:104-108/r9.claim: Al-Nābigha’s poetic use of تجذ illustrates cutting or severing.
TABRISI:11:104-108/r9.anchor: قال النابغة: تجذ السلوقي المضاعف نسجه

TABRISI:11:105#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:105#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:105#3/r2.claim: عطاء is accusative by an implied verb indicated by context: the sense is “He gave them a gift of bliss.”
TABRISI:11:105#3/r2.anchor: وعطاء منصوب بما دل الكلام عليه

TABRISI:11:106-108/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108/r5.speaker: الضحاك والجبائي
TABRISI:11:106-108/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Jubbāʾī take this literally of the transformed skies and earth of the Hereafter, which will not perish when recreated after annihilation.
TABRISI:11:106-108/r5.anchor: أن المراد ما دامت السماوات والأرض مبدلتين

TABRISI:11:106-108/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:106-108/r6.claim: Another view means the skies and earth of Paradise and Hell: everything above is sky and everything under one’s feet is earth; this is close to the first view.
TABRISI:11:106-108/r6.anchor: أن المراد ما دامت سماوات الجنة والنار وأرضهما

TABRISI:11:106-108/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108/r7.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:11:106-108/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the phrase means the Hereafter, which lasts forever, just as the world’s skies and earth endured for the duration of its construction.
TABRISI:11:106-108/r7.anchor: وهي دائمة أبدا كما أن دوام السماء والأرض في الدنيا قدر مدة بنائها عن الحسن

TABRISI:11:106-108/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:106-108/r8.claim: The phrase is an Arabic idiom of perpetuity, not a literal time limit: formulas about night and day, sky and earth, and other supposedly unchanging things mean forever.
TABRISI:11:106-108/r8.anchor: ألفاظا للتبعيد في معنى التأبيد يقولون لا أفعل ذلك ما اختلف الليل والنهار

TABRISI:11:106-108/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108/r9.speaker: عمرو بن معد يكرب
TABRISI:11:106-108/r9.claim: Poetry by ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib uses the two unsetting stars as an image of enduring permanence; Zuhayr similarly speaks of mountains, sky, stars, and lasting days.

TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج والفراء وعلي بن عيسى
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r1.claim: One view makes the exception an increase beyond the stated span: extra punishment for Hell’s people or bliss for Paradise’s; here إلا means سوى, “apart from.”
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r1.anchor: أنه استثناء في الزيادة من العذاب لأهل النار

TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r2.speaker: المازني والبلخي
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r2.claim: Another view applies the exception to time spent at the gathering and judgment or in the barzakh; al-Balkhī prefers this explanation.
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r2.anchor: أن الاستثناء واقع على مقامهم في المحشر والحساب

TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the Hell exception attaches to kinds of torment beyond the two sounds, and the Paradise exception to kinds of bliss; neither limits eternal duration.
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r3.anchor: أن الاستثناء الأول يتصل بقوله { لهم فيها زفير وشهيق }

TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes إلا to mean “and,” adding whatever God wills; grammarians versed in the language weakened this analysis.
TABRISI:11:106-108#2/r4.anchor: أن يكون إلا بمعنى الواو أي وما شاء ربك من الزيادة عن الفراء

TABRISI:11:107-108/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:107-108/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:107-108/r1.claim: The cited poem describes a vanished house whose remaining cold ashes are guarded from wind; al-Farrāʾ reads إلا there as “and.”

TABRISI:11:107-108/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:107-108/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر بن عبد الله وأبو سعيد الخدري وقتادة والسدي والضحاك
TABRISI:11:107-108/r2.claim: This view says monotheist sinners may be punished in Hell and then taken to Paradise by God’s favor; in the Paradise verse the exception is their time in Hell before transfer. ما may mean من for those removed.
TABRISI:11:107-108/r2.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس وجابر بن عبد الله وأبي سعيد الخدري

TABRISI:11:107-108#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:107-108#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:107-108#2/r2.claim: The author selects the interpretation that sinful monotheists may be released from Hell and brought to Paradise, with a corresponding time exception in the Paradise verse.
TABRISI:11:107-108#2/r2.anchor: وهذا القول هو المختار المعول عليه

TABRISI:11:108/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:108/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:108/r1.claim: Those made happy through obedience to God and desisting from sins will be in Paradise.
TABRISI:11:108/r1.anchor: أي سعدوا بطاعة الله وانتهائهم عن المعاصي

TABRISI:11:108/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:108/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:108/r2.claim: All proposed exception readings for Hell apply here except release of sinners from the Fire after entry: those deserving reward enter Paradise and do not leave it.
TABRISI:11:108/r2.anchor: يتأتى فيه جميع ما ذكرنا في الاستثناء من الخلود في النار

TABRISI:11:108/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:108/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:108/r3.claim: عطاء غير مجذوذ means a gift that is never cut off.
TABRISI:11:108/r3.anchor: عطاء غير مجذوذ } أي غير مقطوع

FARRA:v2p27/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p27/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p27/r3.claim: One explanation treats the exception as a resolve God will not enact, like an oath to strike unless one later sees otherwise.
FARRA:v2p27/r3.anchor: أحدهما أن تجعله استثناء يستثنيه ولا يفعله كقولك: والله لأضربنك إلا أن أرى غير ذلك

FARRA:v2p27/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p27/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p27/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ prefers the idiomatic sense “besides”: the stated duration is supplemented by an increase in everlasting life, so the promised gift is not cut off.
FARRA:v2p27/r4.anchor: وهذا أحب الوجهين إلي، لأن الله عز وجل لا خلف لوعده، فقد وصل الاستثناء بقوله (عطاء غير مجذوذ)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p559/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p559/r6.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p559/r6.claim: A group of exegetes says the exception concerns sinful monotheists: they leave Hell for Paradise, or enter Hell temporarily before reaching Paradise; Ibn ʿAbbās gives this sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p559/r6.anchor: وقال جماعة (¬5) من المفسرين: هذا الاستثناء يعود إلى إخراج أهل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p559/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p559/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p559/r7.claim: This interpretation uses “what He wills,” not “whom He wills,” because sinful believers are not the wretched; the wretched are unbelievers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p559/r7.anchor: ولهذا قال: {ما شاء} ولم يقل من شاء؛ لأن المذنبين من المؤمنين لا يكونون أشقياء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p559/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p559/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p559/r8.claim: Abū Isḥāq allows the exception to modify the described sounds of punishment or blessings, leaving other unmentioned kinds of torment or bliss outside the statement.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p559/r8.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬4): ويجوز أن يكون الاستثناء من الزفير والشهيق على أن لهم فيها زفيرا وشهيقا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r1.claim: Saʿida yields saʿāda, saʿd, saʿīd, and means felicity, the opposite of wretchedness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r1.anchor: يقال (¬4) سعد فلان يسعد سعادة وسعدا فهو سعيد نقيض شقي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r2.speaker: أهل الكوفة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r2.claim: The Kufans read saʿidū with a ḍamma on the sīn.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r3.speaker: سيبويه والمحققون من أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r3.claim: Sibawayh and leading linguists say Arabic uses “God made him happy” but does not normally form a passive directly from the intransitive verb; the reading is irregular or analogized to paired intransitive/transitive verbs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r3.anchor: وسيبويه والمحققون من أهل اللغة على أن كلام العرب (أسعده الله) وأنه لا يبني في الثلاثة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r4.speaker: المحققون من أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r4.claim: They reject “masʿūd” as conclusive proof of a passive سعد, since forms like majnūn and maḥbūb can drop an augment; cited poetry likewise shows augment deletion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r4.anchor: هذا كلام المحققين من أهل اللغة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r5.claim: On that account, saʿidū itself could derive from asʿadahu Allāh with the augment omitted, as in masʿūd.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r5.anchor: ثم يمكن أن يقال: {سعدوا} أيضا من أسعده الله، وقد جاء على حذف الزيادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج والفارابي والأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r6.claim: Later linguists allow both saʿdahu and asʿadahu; al-Zajjāj, al-Fārābī, and al-Azharī each cite the forms or meanings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r6.anchor: والمتأخرون أجازوا: سعده الله وأسعده، فقد ذكر الزجاج (¬4) في باب الوفاق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r7.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says Arabs say saʿida for the person and asʿadahu for God, while Hudhayl uses saʿida with ḍamma and Ibn Masʿūd's companions read accordingly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء (¬2): كلام العرب سعد الرجل وأسعده الله، إلا هذيلا فإنهم يقولون: سعد الرجل بالضم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r8.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p562#2/r8.claim: Al-Kisāʾī treats saʿidū and asʿidū as two dialectal forms.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p565/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p565/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p565/r1.claim: ʿAṭāʾ is an accusative verbal noun supplied by the sense of the preceding clause (“giving them bliss”), or a noun used in place of a verbal noun; al-Qaṭāmī illustrates the latter use.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p565/r1.anchor: انتصب (عطاء) على المصدر بما دل عليه الأول، كأنه قيل: إعطاهم النعيم عطاء غير مجذوذ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p565/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p565/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p565/r2.claim: All commentators take majdhūdh to mean cut off; the root means cutting, as in the expression “may God cut off their rear.” Al-Nābigha's verse is also cited.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p565/r2.anchor: قول المفسرين (¬6) كلهم، يقال: جذّه يجذّه جذّا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p565/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p565/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p565/r3.claim: The verse indicates that the people of Paradise will enjoy blessings that never end.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p565/r3.anchor: والآية تدل على أن نعيم أهل الجنة لا ينقطع أبدا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210/r1.claim: The exception and duration in this clause are explained in his book al-Mushkil; no further gloss is given here.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210/r1.anchor: خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك} مبين في كتاب "المشكل" (1) .
