IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#2/r1.claim: Ghayr majdhūdh means uncut or unsevered; jadadta, jadhadta, jadhafta, and jadafta are all said for cutting.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#2/r1.anchor: غير مجذوذ} أي: غير مقطوع. يقال: جذذت، وجددت وجذفت، وجدفت؛ إذا قطعت.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:108-109/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:108-109/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:108-109/r1.claim: An unsevered gift is uncut and uninterrupted.

ELMALILI:11:108-109/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r1.claim: The blessed remain in Paradise as long as heaven and earth endure, meaning without end.
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r1.anchor: semâvât ve arz dâim oldukça -yani ilâ gayri’n-nihâye- cümlesi orada muhalled olarak

ELMALILI:11:108-109/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r2.claim: The exception means everlastingness is neither necessary in itself nor natural; its continuance depends on God's will.
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r2.anchor: devam ve hulûd da vücûb-i zâtî ile vâcib ve tabîî değil Allah’ın meşiyyetiyledir

ELMALILI:11:108-109/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r3.claim: One possible exception is that sinful believers are not initially counted among the blessed: they remain in Hell for a time before entering Paradise.
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r3.anchor: Nitekim usât-ı mü’minîn doğrudan doğru cennete girmeyecek, bidâyeten mes‘ud olmayıp bir müddet cehennemde kalacaktır

ELMALILI:11:108-109/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r4.claim: Another possibility is that God grants some specially chosen people a bliss surpassing Paradise, including divine pleasure and vision.
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r4.anchor: bir kısım bahtiyarlar cennetten daha ileri yükselerek

ELMALILI:11:108-109/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r5.claim: This is a gift that never ceases, unlike earthly provision bounded by a fixed term.
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r5.anchor: dünyadaki gibi bir ecel-i ma‘dûd ile mahdud ve mütenâhî değil, lâyenkatı‘devam eden bir atâ

ELMALILI:11:108-109/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r6.claim: The phrase may be parsed as a circumstantial accusative describing the blessed abiding in Paradise; on this reading, Paradise's delights plainly do not cease.
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r6.anchor: Bu kayıt, ya فَفِى ٱلْجَنَّةِ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا’dan hâl veya مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ’den temyizdir

ELMALILI:11:108-109/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r7.claim: Alternatively, it is a specification of the exception; this directly makes the higher bliss of divine pleasure uninterrupted and also signals Paradise's endlessness.
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r7.anchor: Temyiz olduğu takdirde ise cennetin fevkinde olan ve müstesnâ bir surette meşiyyet-i ilâhiye ta‘alluk eden na‘îm-i rıdvânın ‘adem-i inkıtâ‘ında bilhassa sarih

ELMALILI:11:108-109/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r8.claim: Because the afterlife certainly contains an unending gift, it must itself be eternal; the encompassing heavens and earth therefore endure forever, explaining the duration phrase.
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r8.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh عَطَآءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍۢ işaretiyle مَا دَامَتِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلْأَرْضُ’ın ebediyetini tefsir eder

ELMALILI:11:108-109/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r9.claim: It is incorrect to infer that reward is eternal while punishment in general must end, since the next verse explicitly states that the gift is unbroken.
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r9.anchor: bazılarının sevap ebedî fakat azab umûmiyetle munkatı‘olacaktır zannetmeleri doğru değildir

ELMALILI:11:108-109/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r10.claim: Those who seek worldly life receive their full allotted worldly share, then have only Fire and remain wretched; believers who humble themselves before God abide happily in Paradise.
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r10.anchor: İşte iki fırka arasındaki fark bu kadar büyüktür

ELMALILI:11:108-109/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r11.claim: The leaders of the wretched, like Pharaoh and his entourage, receive a specially willed torment within Hell whose painful terror cannot be conveyed even by fire.
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r11.anchor: azab vardır ki bunun dehşet-i âlâmı ateş ile bile ifade ve ihsas edilemez

ELMALILI:11:108-109/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r12.claim: The leaders of the blessed, such as prophets and the truthful, receive a special joy beyond Paradise's ordinary blessings, sheer divine grace beyond all earned reward.
ELMALILI:11:108-109/r12.anchor: bütün nimetlerin, istihkākların fevkinde mahz-ı fazl-ı rabbânî olan bir atâ-i gayr-i meczuzdur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r1.claim: These verses explain the gathering described in 11:103 and portray the Last Day by showing people's outcomes and destinations according to worldly faith and deeds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r1.anchor: Bu âyetler, 103. âyetin “O gün bütün insanların bir araya toplandığı gündür” meâlindeki bölümünü açıklayıcı mahiyette olup

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r4.claim: People will be divided in the afterlife into the wretched and the happy according to their faith and deeds in this world.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r4.anchor: İnsanlar, dünyadaki iman ve amellerine göre âhirette bedbahtlar ve mutlular olmak üzere iki gruba ayrılacaklardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r6.claim: The happy, meaning believers, will be rewarded with the blessings of Paradise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r6.anchor: 108. âyette ise mutluların yani müminlerin cennet nimetleriyle ödüllendirilecekleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r13.claim: The happy will live forever in Paradise; despite the exception, the verse's final phrase establishes uninterrupted blessings and no removal from Paradise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r13.anchor: ancak âyetin son cümlesi cennet nimetlerinin kesintisiz olduğunu ve cennete girenlerin oradan çıkarılmayacağını göstermektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r14.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r14.claim: Ibn Ashur's first reading is that unrepentant believers spend time in Hell, then God's mercy forgives them and admits them to Paradise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r14.anchor: İbn Âşûr’a göre bu istisna iki anlamda yorumlanabilir: ☼1. Tövbe etmeden âhirete giden müminler bir süre cehennemde

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r15.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r15.claim: Ibn Ashur's second reading is that the exception prevents Paradise's merciful blessings from being understood as a debt God owes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r15.anchor: İbn Âşûr’a göre bu istisna iki anlamda yorumlanabilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r16.speaker: Reşîd Rızâ
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r16.claim: Rashid Rida is cited for reading the exception as God willing to bestow another reward on the inhabitants of Paradise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r16.anchor: Bazı müfessirlerse bu istisnayı, “Allah onlara başka bir mükâfat bahşetmeyi istemedikçe” şeklinde yorumlamışlardır (Reşîd Rızâ

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r17.speaker: Esed
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r17.claim: Esed reports a reading in which the exception means God may open a new evolutionary scene or higher stage for people in Paradise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:105/r17.anchor: “Allah insanın önünde yeni bir evrim sahnesi, daha yüksek bir evre açmadıkça (cennette sonsuz olarak kalacaklardır)” şeklinde yorumlayanlar da vardır (Esed, 447).

BURHAN:v3p48#2/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p48#2/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p48#2/r5.claim: The exception for the happy in Paradise is followed by an unbroken gift, which removes any suggestion that their abiding or God's gift will end.
BURHAN:v3p48#2/r5.anchor: ولما علم أن أهل السعادة لا خروج لهم من الجنة أكد خلودهم بعد الاستثناء بما يرفع أصل الاستثناء

BURHAN:v2p402/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p402/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p402/r3.claim: The abiding phrase is a confirmatory circumstantial qualifier for the happy people's being in Paradise; this resolves the apparent rule that a circumstantial qualifier must describe a changing state, which applies only to non-confirmatory qualifiers.
BURHAN:v2p402/r3.anchor: فانه حال مؤكدة لقوله ﴿ وأما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة خالدين فيها ﴾ وبهذا يزول الاشكال

BURHAN:v2p402/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p402/r4.speaker: ابن جنى
BURHAN:v2p402/r4.claim: Because he did not recognize the confirmatory type, Ibn Jinni supplied an omitted phrase meaning they believe they will abide there, treating that belief as a fixed state.
BURHAN:v2p402/r4.anchor: ولما لم يقف ابن جنى على ذلك قدر محذوفا أي معتقدا خلودهم فيها

BURHAN:v3p50/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p50/r1.speaker: بعض الصحابة
BURHAN:v3p50/r1.claim: Some Companions hope the exception means the people of Paradise move to a higher station, such as divine pleasure or vision; the Prophet approved this hope.
BURHAN:v3p50/r1.anchor: قول بعض 2 الصحابة وإنا لنرجو فوق ذلك مظهرا وصوبه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BURHAN:v3p50/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p50/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v3p50/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the first exception as people of Hell moving to extreme cold or another punishment, and the second as major sinners' rescue from punishment.
BURHAN:v3p50/r2.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري الاستثناء الأول لخروج أهل النار إلى الزمهرير أو إلى نوع آخر من العذاب

BURHAN:v3p50/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p50/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v3p50/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari argues by symmetry: since Paradise's exception cannot terminate bliss in light of the uncut gift, Hell's exception likewise cannot terminate punishment.
BURHAN:v3p50/r3.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري الاستثناء الأول لخروج أهل النار إلى الزمهرير أو إلى نوع آخر من العذاب

BURHAN:v3p50/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p50/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p50/r4.claim: The author keeps the first exception at its apparent sense, taking it as deliverance from Hell; there is no reason to abandon the ordinary force of exception.
BURHAN:v3p50/r4.anchor: ظاهر الاستثناء هو الإخراج عن حكم ما قبله ولا موجب للعدول عن الظاهر في الاستثناء الأول فحمل على النجاة

BURHAN:v3p50/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p50/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p50/r5.claim: God's doing what He wills explains both punishment and gracious rescue; the uncut gift clarifies that the second exception does not end Paradise's bliss.
BURHAN:v3p50/r5.anchor: من العذاب والإنجاء منه بفضله ولا يتوجه عليه اعتراض أحد

BURHAN:v3p50/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p50/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p50/r6.claim: The author rejects al-Zamakhshari's symmetry as strained: the second exception is not literal, so it does not require the first to depart from its apparent meaning.
BURHAN:v3p50/r6.anchor: ورعاية هذا الباب أولى من رعاية الباب الذي توهم الزمخشري

NAHHAS:v2p302/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p302/r10.speaker: الأعمش وحمزة والكسائي
NAHHAS:v2p302/r10.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī read the sīn with ḍamma, سُعِدوا.
NAHHAS:v2p302/r10.anchor:
وقرأ الأعمش وحمزة والكسائي
108
بضم السين

NAHHAS:v2p302/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p302/r11.speaker: أبو عمرو
NAHHAS:v2p302/r11.claim: Abū ʿAmr favors active سعدوا, reasoning that the earlier clause says شقوا rather than أُشْقوا.
NAHHAS:v2p302/r11.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو والدليل على أنه سعدوا أن الأول شقوا ولم يقل أشقوا

NAHHAS:v2p302/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p302/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p302/r12.claim: Abū Jaʿfar endorses ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān's objection that al-Kisāʾī's reading is ungrammatical: سعد is intransitive, while God makes someone happy with أسعد.
NAHHAS:v2p302/r12.anchor: رأيت علي بن سليمان يتعجب من قراءة الكسائي ( سعدوا ) مع علمه بالعربية إذ كان هذا لحنا لا يجوز لأنه إنما يقال سعد فلان وأسعده الله جل وعز

NAHHAS:v2p302/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p302/r13.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v2p302/r13.claim: Al-Kisāʾī cites مسعود and several Arab verb pairs as support; Abū Jaʿfar rejects these as isolated usages that cannot establish a productive rule.
NAHHAS:v2p302/r13.anchor: إنما احتج الكسائي بقولهم مسعود ولا حجة له فيه لأنه يقال مكان مسعود فيه ثم يحذف فيه

NAHHAS:v2p302/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p302/r14.speaker: علي بن سليمان
NAHHAS:v2p302/r14.claim: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān says a transitive form of فغر فوه would be أفغرت فاه; Abū Jaʿfar accepts this as a separate dialect, not a general rule.
NAHHAS:v2p302/r14.anchor: سمعت علي بن سليمان يقول لو قال لنا قائل كيف تنطقون بالمتعدي من فغر فوه ما قلنا إلا أفغرت فاه وهذا الذي قال حسن

NAHHAS:v2p302/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p302/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p302/r15.claim: عطاء is a verbal noun, and غير مجذوذ is its adjective.
NAHHAS:v2p302/r15.anchor: ( عطاء ) اسم للمصدر ( غير مجذوذ ) من نعته يقال جذه وحذه

NAHHAS:v2p302/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p302/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p302/r16.claim: The verbs جذّه and حذّه mean to cut; an unattributed poem illustrates جذّ, and the source names no poet.
NAHHAS:v2p302/r16.anchor: يقال جذه وحذه كما قال ( تجذ السلوقي المضاعف نسجه … ويوقدن بالصفاح نار الحباحب )

ITQAN:v2p314#2/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p314#2/r19.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p314#2/r19.claim: Ghayra majdūdh means uncut or unending.

ITQAN:v3p177/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p177/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p177/r3.claim: Verbal emphasis may repeat a synonym, as in ḍayqan ḥarajan and gharābību sūd; al-Saffar also treats fīmā in makkannākum fīhi as two negations.
ITQAN:v3p177/r3.anchor: ثانيها التأكيد اللفظي وهو تكرار اللفظ الأول إما بمرادفه نحو

DAMGHANI:v1p103/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p103/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p103/r4.claim: Jadhdh can mean diminution or cutting off; the gift is neither diminished nor cut off.
DAMGHANI:v1p103/r4.anchor: فوجه منهما الجذ النقص والقطع قوله تعالى في سورة هود

BURHAN:v4p242/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p242/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p242/r1.claim: أما can elaborate a summary, as when the fates of two groups detail that people are gathered; it can also restrict an assertion to one claimed attribute.
BURHAN:v4p242/r1.anchor: وتذكر لتفصيل ما أجمله المخاطب وللاقتصار على بعض ما ادعى

BURHAN:v2p386/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p386/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p386/r7.claim: Repetition can occur in a genitive construction; the repeated element is usually attached to the expression it reiterates.
BURHAN:v2p386/r7.anchor: يكون في المجرور كقوله ﴿ وأما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة خالدين فيها ﴾ 6 والأكثر فيه اتصاله بالمذكور

BURHAN:v2p386/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p386/r8.speaker: الكوفيون
BURHAN:v2p386/r8.claim: The Kūfans say an emphatic element cannot be separated from what it emphasizes; al-Ṣaffār rejects this against transmitted usage, citing pronouns, repeated لما, and repeated أنكم.
BURHAN:v2p386/r8.anchor: وزعم الكوفيون انه لا يجوز الفصل بين التوكيد المؤكد قال الصفار في شرح سيبويه والسماع يرده

BURHAN:v4p57/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p57/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p57/r2.claim: Although the heavens and earth do not end, the permanence formula follows Arab custom, which uses their duration to express eternity in both reward and punishment.
BURHAN:v4p57/r2.anchor: مع أنهما لايزولان لكن التقييد بالسماء والأرض جرت عادة العرب إذا قصدوا الدوام أن يعلقوا بهما فجاء الخطاب على ذلك

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r1.claim: Arabic uses enduring conditions such as night and day differing, the sea rising, a mountain standing, or heaven and earth enduring to mean forever.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r1.anchor: فإن للعرب في معنى (الأبد) ألفاظا يستعملونها في كلامهم، يقولون: لا أفعل ذلك ما اختلف الليل والنهار

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r2.claim: He first interprets the duration as the lifetime of the world, since heaven and earth will change at the end; the exception allows added duration beyond that term.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r2.anchor: وللسماء وللأرض وقت يتغيران فيه عن هيئتهما

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r3.claim: غير مجذوذ means uncut off or uninterrupted.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r4.claim: Here إلا means سوى, as in the idiom of staying a year in a house except for whatever one wills to add to the year.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r4.anchor: و (إلا) في هذا الموضع بمعنى (سوى) ومثله من الكلام: لأسكنن في هذه الدار حولا إلا ما شئت

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r5.claim: A second interpretation takes the expression as the Arabs' conventional word for eternity and the exception as the people's time on earth before they entered Paradise or Hell.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r5.anchor: وفيه (قول آخر) ، وهو: أن يجعل دوام السماء والأرض بمعنى الأبد

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r6.claim: A third interpretation makes the exception the sinful Muslims' time in Hell until God's mercy and the Prophet's intercession remove them to Paradise; the garden's exception likewise covers their prior stay in Hell.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53/r6.anchor: وفيه (وجه ثالث) : وهو أن يكون الاستثناء من الخلود

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r3.claim: One explanation is that the exception covers those still awaiting judgment, because reckoning is unfinished and neither the saved nor the damned have yet entered their final abode.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r3.anchor: الحساب لم ينته بعد ولم يكن أهل الجنة في الجنة ولا أهل النار في النار فاستثنى منهم من في الحساب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r5.claim: Another explanation says that God's pleasure and the vision of His noble face are greater than Paradise and its delights.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r5.anchor: أما أهل الجنة فهناك ما هو أكبر من الجنة ونعيمها وهو رضوان الله تعالى والنظر إلى وجهه الكريم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r6.speaker: قسم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r6.claim: Some take the exception to mean the period spent at the gathering place, described here as fifty thousand years.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r6.anchor: قسم يقولون أن الإستثناء هو في مدة المكث في الحشر (مدته خمسين ألف سنة)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r7.speaker: قسم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r7.claim: Some explain it as the time until God finishes judging among all creatures.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r7.anchor: وقسم من قال هذا حتى يقضي الله تعالى بين الخلائق

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r9.speaker: قسم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r9.claim: Some take it as an exception for the period in the grave and the time before leaving this world.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r9.anchor: وقسم قال الاستثناء من بقائهم في القبر وخروجهم من الدنيا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r10.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r10.speaker: قسم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r10.claim: Some take it as an exception for remaining in worldly life.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r10.anchor: وقسم قال هو استثناء من البقاء في الدنيا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r11.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r11.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r11.claim: The proposed meanings may all be intended: the exception can cover the decreed time before entry, while the final decree still makes them everlasting.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p587/r11.anchor: وهذه المعاني كلها قد تكون مرادة وتفيد أنهم خالدين فيها إلا المدة التي قضاها الله تعالى قبل أن يدخلوا الجنة

NASHR:v2p290/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p290/r7.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص والباقون
NASHR:v2p290/r7.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, Khalaf, and Hafs read the sīn in سعدوا with ḍamma; the others use fatḥa.
NASHR:v2p290/r7.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص بضم السين
